en.explanation: It automates Interconnect Gateways in the provider fabric and private links to AWS, Azure or Google, and site-to-site via the provider.

en.question: What is the most common way to deploy Catalyst SD-WAN controllers today?
options: On the Meraki dashboard
On every branch router
Inside the customer's ISE nodes
Cisco-hosted cloud controllers
en.explanation: Cisco (or a partner) hosts Manager, Validator and Controllers in the cloud, giving quick setup and managed operations; on-prem is also possible.

en.question: Which hypervisors can host on-premises SD-WAN controllers?
options: The router's Guest Shell
Only Microsoft Hyper-V
Docker Desktop on a laptop
VMware ESXi and KVM
en.explanation: Controllers ship as OVA/qcow2 images for ESXi and KVM, and are also available in public clouds (AWS, Azure).

en.question: When installing controllers on-prem, which settings must be configured on each before they can join the fabric?
options: Only a hostname and a default route in VPN 0
System IP, site ID, org name, Validator
The OMP hold timers and the BFD intervals
A WLAN profile and RF profile
en.explanation: Each controller needs system-ip, site-id, organization-name, the vbond address and a VPN 0 transport interface, plus certificates.

en.question: How is the SD-WAN Manager scaled for many devices and made redundant?
options: More BFD sessions per tunnel
A second Validator in the same site
A cluster of Manager nodes
A larger MTU on VPN 0
en.explanation: Manager clusters (typically 3 or 6 nodes) share the load and data; Validators and Controllers are scaled by adding more instances.

en.question: How many Controllers does each WAN Edge connect to by default?
options: One, with no option to change
Two (max-control-connections)
Every Controller in the overlay
None, it only uses the Validator
en.explanation: By default edges keep two control connections per transport to different Controllers for redundancy; this is tunable.

en.question: Why must a WAN Edge's serial number be in the Manager's device list (WAN Edge list) before it joins?
options: It tells the router which LAN VLANs to create
It sets the speed of the device's WAN link
It chooses the colour of every TLOC
Only listed devices are accepted
en.explanation: The authorised serial/chassis list is synced from the Plug and Play portal and pushed to Validators and Controllers; unknown devices are rejected.

en.question: Controllers fail to authenticate each other after a new enterprise CA was introduced. What is the likely cause?
options: OMP graceful restart is disabled
The new root CA is missing on some nodes
The BFD multiplier is too low on the hubs
The colour on VPN 0 is 'default'
en.explanation: With enterprise certificates, every controller and edge must trust the root CA chain; otherwise DTLS/TLS authentication fails.

en.question: Which command on an IOS XE WAN Edge shows the state of its DTLS control connections?
options: show interface status
show sdwan omp routes summary
show sdwan control connections
show crypto pki trustpoints
en.explanation: show sdwan control connections (and control local-properties, connection-history) shows peers, state and errors.

en.question: show sdwan control connection-history shows error CRTVERFL. What does it point to?
options: OMP has no routes
The tunnel MTU is too small for the payload
Certificate check failed
The TLOC colour is invalid
en.explanation: CRTVERFL is a certificate verification failure (e.g. untrusted root, expired or wrong serial); check certificates and time (NTP).

en.question: A new edge cannot reach the Validator by its FQDN. What should you check first?
options: The QoS map on the tunnel
The OSPF area on the LAN side
DNS and VPN 0 routing
The firewall policy in VPN 10
en.explanation: Control connections start from VPN 0 (transport); the edge needs a route and working DNS to resolve and reach the Validator.

en.question: How does a new WAN Edge on a DHCP internet link find its controllers with zero-touch?
options: It scans the internet for open SD-WAN ports
It waits for an engineer to type the config on the console
It asks PnP Connect, which points it to the Validator
It copies the config from the nearest edge by Bluetooth
en.explanation: ZTP/PnP: the device gets an address, reaches devicehelper/PnP cloud, learns its Validator and organisation and then downloads its config.

en.question: When is bootstrap (a generated config file) used instead of ZTP?
options: When PnP cannot be reached
When the device has more than two WAN links
When the device runs an older BFD version
When the site uses OSPF on the LAN
en.explanation: A bootstrap file from the Manager (on USB or flash) provides the initial transport settings and identity where ZTP is not possible.

en.question: Why deploy two WAN Edges in a data centre or regional hub?
options: To avoid using any Controllers
To double the number of OMP routes per prefix
Because each edge supports only one VPN
Redundancy and capacity
en.explanation: Hubs aggregate many tunnels; dual edges with LAN-side routing (BGP/OSPF, VRRP) give resilience and scale.

en.question: A branch has two edges, each with only one of the two WAN circuits. How can both edges use both circuits?
options: TLOC extension between the two edges
OMP graceful restart on the circuits
A second Validator at the branch
Cloud OnRamp for SaaS on one edge
en.explanation: TLOC extension links the routers so each can build tunnels over the circuit terminated on its peer.

en.question: What are on-demand (dynamic) tunnels in SD-WAN?
options: Spoke-to-spoke tunnels built when needed
Tunnels that change colour every hour
Tunnels between controllers only
Backup tunnels that use only the 4G/LTE link
en.explanation: With on-demand tunnels, spokes use the hub by default and bring up direct tunnels when traffic flows, saving resources on small devices.

en.question: Two edges use 'private' colours (mpls) on one side and 'public' (biz-internet) on the other. When do tunnels use public IPs?
options: Never, tunnels always use private IPs
When a public colour is involved
Only when restrict is set on both colours
Only for traffic in VPN 0
en.explanation: Edges use private (pre-NAT) addresses between private colours and post-NAT public addresses when a public colour is involved.

en.question: What does the 'restrict' keyword on a TLOC colour do?
options: Limits the link to 10 Mb/s
Blocks all control connections on that link
Stops BFD on that colour
Tunnels only to the same colour
en.explanation: restrict prevents tunnels to other colours, for example keeping MPLS traffic only between MPLS TLOCs.

en.question: How does OMP choose the best route when several edges advertise the same prefix?
options: The edge with the highest serial number wins
Preference, TLOC preference, origin
The route learned first is always kept forever
OMP picks one at random each minute
en.explanation: OMP best path compares preference, TLOC preference, origin type and metric, among others; control policy can change these attributes.

en.question: By default, which LAN routes does an edge advertise into OMP?
options: No routes until a policy is applied
BGP and OSPF routes only
Connected and static routes
Only the default route
en.explanation: Connected and static are redistributed by default; OSPF, BGP and EIGRP must be enabled under OMP advertise.

en.question: Why set a higher TLOC preference on the MPLS colour at a hub?
options: It encrypts the MPLS tunnel twice
Remote sites prefer that TLOC
It gives the MPLS link more bandwidth
It disables the internet TLOC
en.explanation: TLOC preference influences OMP path choice for remote edges; higher is preferred.

en.question: In SD-WAN Manager, how is a device template built from feature templates?
options: It is created automatically by the Validator after ZTP
It is a single text file copied from another vendor's router
It combines feature templates
It contains only the device serial number and licence
en.explanation: Device templates reference feature templates; device-specific values are filled in through variables when attaching.

en.question: When would you use a CLI add-on template?
options: To push a firmware image to all edges at the same time
To replace OMP with a CLI-only routing protocol on every edge
For a few commands that no feature template supports
To create the certificate signing request for the Validator
en.explanation: The CLI add-on adds raw CLI to a feature-based device template, avoiding a full CLI template for small gaps.

en.question: A branch has two edges serving one LAN. Which protocol gives hosts a single default gateway?
options: Cloud OnRamp for SaaS with a gateway site
OMP on the service VPN between the two edges
BFD
VRRP
en.explanation: VRRP on the service-side interfaces provides a virtual gateway; it can track OMP or interfaces.

en.question: A hub edge learns OSPF routes from the DC and must advertise them to branches. What is required?
options: Configure OSPF in VPN 512 so the Manager can see it
Nothing, OSPF routes are sent into OMP by default with all their LSAs
Run OSPF between all edges across the internet links
Advertise OSPF into OMP in the service VPN
en.explanation: OSPF must be redistributed into OMP (omp advertise ospf) in that VPN; also redistribute OMP into OSPF for the reverse path.

en.question: Edges redistribute OMP into BGP at a DC that also has MPLS CE routers. What prevents a routing loop?
options: Route tagging or BGP communities with filters
Raising the BFD hello interval on every tunnel in the overlay
Disabling OMP graceful restart on the hub
Using GRE instead of IPsec on all of the tunnels
en.explanation: Mutual redistribution at multiple points needs tags/communities (or SoO, AS-path) to stop routes learned from the overlay coming back.

en.question: Where can EIGRP be used on a Catalyst SD-WAN edge?
options: Only in VPN 0 to reach the Validator over the internet
As the overlay protocol between all edges instead of OMP
On the service side, redistributed into OMP
Only between the Manager cluster nodes
en.explanation: EIGRP is supported on IOS XE SD-WAN service VPNs and can be advertised into OMP like OSPF or BGP.

en.question: How is multicast handled in Catalyst SD-WAN overlay?
options: Multicast is not supported in any SD-WAN release
Every edge floods multicast to all other edges in every VPN
Replicators copy traffic to receivers' edges
The Controller forwards the multicast data itself
en.explanation: Edges run PIM on the service side; OMP signals joins and designated replicators reduce the head-end replication load.

en.question: What are configuration groups in SD-WAN Manager?
options: A newer model built from feature profiles
A list of administrators allowed to change the overlay settings
Groups of BFD sessions that share timers
The Validator's list of authorised serials
en.explanation: Configuration groups (with system, transport, service and policy profiles) and guided workflows simplify the older template model.

en.question: Where is a centralized control policy applied?
options: On the Controller, to OMP routes and TLOCs
On each edge's LAN interface as an access list for all traffic
On the Validator for NAT traversal
On the Manager's GUI login page
en.explanation: Control policies run on Controllers and change what OMP routes/TLOCs are advertised to which sites, building topologies such as hub-and-spoke.

en.question: A control policy for hub-and-spoke sets the spokes' routes' TLOC to the hub. What is the effect?
options: Spoke-to-spoke traffic goes through the hub
Spokes lose all routes to the data centre and to each other
BFD stops on all tunnels to the hub site
The hub becomes the Validator for the region
en.explanation: By setting the next-hop TLOC (or filtering spoke TLOCs), spokes reach each other via the hub instead of direct tunnels.

en.question: What does a centralized data policy act on?
options: Only OMP routes reflected by the Controller to the sites
Traffic matched by ports or DSCP
The Manager's scheduled database backups
Certificates on the edges
en.explanation: Data policies are defined on the Controller but enforced on edges: match packet fields, then drop, set next hop, TLOC, NAT, etc.

en.question: Which policy type is configured on the edge itself, such as an interface ACL or QoS?
options: VPN membership policy
Centralized control policy pushed via OMP to all sites
Application-aware routing policy on the Validator
Localized policy
en.explanation: Localized policies (ACLs, QoS, route policies) are attached to device templates/config groups and run locally.

en.question: What is a VPN in Catalyst SD-WAN?
options: A single tunnel between two edges
An IPsec remote-access client for laptops on the road
A segment like a VRF, tagged in the data plane
A group of Manager users with the same role
en.explanation: Service VPNs (1–511 etc.) are isolated routing tables; the VPN label travels in packets so segments stay separate end to end.

en.question: Which VPN is reserved for the transport (WAN) side?
options: VPN 512, also used for the out-of-band management port
VPN 1
VPN 0
en.explanation: VPN 0 is transport; VPN 512 is out-of-band management; service VPNs carry user traffic.

en.question: Guest traffic (VPN 20) must reach only the internet via the DC, never other VPNs. Which approach fits?
options: Use the same VPN for guests and staff with an ACL
Put guest users in VPN 0 so that they share the transport interface
Disable BFD for VPN 20 on every branch
A topology policy for VPN 20 to the DC hub
en.explanation: Per-VPN topologies (hub-and-spoke for VPN 20) plus keeping VPN separation give isolation; route leaking is only done if explicitly configured.

en.question: What does application-aware routing do?
options: Picks tunnels meeting an app's SLA class
Assigns a separate VPN to each application automatically
Blocks applications that are not in the list
Compresses application traffic
en.explanation: AAR uses BFD measurements of loss, latency and jitter against SLA classes and moves traffic when a path breaks the SLA.

en.question: No path meets the voice SLA class. What happens with a default AAR policy without 'strict'?
options: Traffic still uses an available path
Voice traffic is dropped at the branch until a path recovers
The edge reboots to reset BFD
The Controller blocks all OMP routes for that site
en.explanation: Without strict, traffic falls back to available paths (or the configured fallback/backup colour); strict drops it.

en.question: What does Enhanced AAR improve over classic AAR?
options: Faster SLA detection with inline data
It removes the need for SLA classes in all policies
It runs on the Validator instead of the edges
It turns off BFD to save bandwidth
en.explanation: Enhanced AAR uses inline data-plane measurements for sub-second detection; Predictive Path Recommendations use analytics to suggest better preferences.

en.question: How is direct internet access (DIA) usually done at a branch?
options: Backhauling every flow to the DC first through IPsec
NAT on VPN 0 plus a route or policy
Turning off the IPsec tunnels at that branch
Using VPN 512 for user traffic
en.explanation: DIA enables NAT on the VPN 0 interface and sends chosen traffic there with a service-VPN NAT route or a centralized data policy.

en.question: What does service insertion (service chaining) do?
options: Inserts the Manager GUI into each branch router as a container
Steers chosen traffic through a firewall or IPS
Adds a second Controller to every region
Replaces OMP with static routes
en.explanation: Edges advertise services (FW, IDS, netsvc) in OMP; policies set traffic to traverse them, often at a hub.

en.question: What is the application-aware enterprise firewall on SD-WAN edges?
options: A cloud-only firewall that needs SIG on every branch link
A zone-based stateful firewall that matches apps
A stateless ACL applied on the VPN 0 interface
A firewall that only inspects OMP
en.explanation: It is IOS XE zone-based firewall with NBAR application matching, configured as a security policy in the Manager.

en.question: Where do IPS, URL filtering and AMP run on an IOS XE SD-WAN edge?
options: In a security virtual image (UTD container)
On the Validator, which inspects all user traffic for every site
On the Manager cluster nodes in the data centre
In the BFD process of the data plane
en.explanation: UTD (Snort-based) runs as a container on the router; the image must match the IOS XE version and the platform needs enough memory.

en.question: A URL filtering policy blocks gambling sites. How are sites classified?
options: By web reputation and category
By the source IP address of each user on the LAN
By the TLOC colour of the link
By the OMP route tags sent by the Controller
en.explanation: URL filtering uses Talos categories and reputation scores, with allow/block lists for exceptions.

en.question: What does AMP do on an SD-WAN edge?
options: Encrypts management traffic between the edge and Manager
Measures latency for AAR on every tunnel
Checks file reputation and blocks known malware
Assigns QoS classes
en.explanation: Advanced Malware Protection looks up file hashes in the cloud and can send unknown files to Threat Grid for analysis.

en.question: Why enable the SSL/TLS proxy on edges with IPS and URL filtering?
options: To encrypt BFD probes, which are sent in clear text by default
To inspect inside encrypted flows
To replace IPsec on the overlay
To speed up control connections
en.explanation: Most traffic is HTTPS; the proxy decrypts (with a CA trusted by clients) so UTD can inspect, then re-encrypts.

en.question: How does TrustSec integrate with Catalyst SD-WAN?
options: It is not supported on any edge
By replacing every VPN with a separate SGT in the Manager database
By using SGTs as TLOC colours
SGTs carried inline across the overlay
en.explanation: Edges can propagate SGT in the data plane (or learn via SXP) and enforce identity-based policy (SGACL, firewall).

en.question: How does Umbrella DNS security work on an SD-WAN edge?
options: Umbrella replaces BFD
The edge resolves every name locally from a downloaded list of domains
The Validator answers all DNS queries
The edge redirects DNS queries to Umbrella
en.explanation: The edge intercepts DNS (DNS redirect) and sends it to Umbrella with device/VPN identity, blocking malicious domains.

en.question: How do branch edges send internet traffic to a Secure Internet Gateway (SIG)?
options: Only by backhauling traffic to the DC and from there to a proxy server
Auto IPsec/GRE tunnels to the SIG
By changing the DNS server of each PC
Through OMP to the Controller
en.explanation: SIG templates/features build tunnels to Umbrella/Secure Access or third-party SIGs, and routes/policy send traffic into them.

en.question: How many forwarding queues does a Catalyst SD-WAN IOS XE edge use for QoS on an interface?
options: Eight (queue 0 is low latency)
Two, one for control and one for all other data
Sixteen per tunnel interface
One shared queue for all classes
en.explanation: There are eight queues; queue 0 is the LLQ, others share bandwidth by weight; class maps tie classes to queues.

en.question: Which queuing method protects voice with a strict priority queue?
options: FIFO
Weighted random early detection applied to the default queue
LLQ
Round-robin across tunnels
en.explanation: Low Latency Queuing serves the priority queue first (policed to avoid starvation), others get CBWFQ shares.

en.question: A branch has a 100 Mb/s port but a 20 Mb/s internet contract. What is needed for QoS to work?
options: Marking all traffic EF
Policing incoming traffic to 100 Mb/s on the LAN interfaces
A higher BFD multiplier
Shaping to 20 Mb/s
en.explanation: Without shaping, the queue builds in the provider network; shaping to the contract makes the edge's queues take effect.

en.question: What does a policer do to traffic above its rate?
options: Drops or re-marks it
Buffers it until the link is idle and then sends it in order
Sends it over a different VPN
Encrypts it again
en.explanation: Policing does not queue: excess traffic is dropped or re-marked; shaping buffers instead.

en.question: Where is DSCP for overlay traffic copied so the underlay provider can honour it?
options: Nowhere, it is lost
To the OMP route attributes for each of the prefixes
To the BFD session ID
To the outer IPsec/GRE header
en.explanation: Edges copy (or rewrite) the inner DSCP to the tunnel's outer header so the transport can apply its own QoS.

en.question: What problem does per-tunnel QoS solve at a hub?
options: Spokes exceeding the number of OMP routes allowed by the Controller
A hub overrunning small spoke links
BFD sessions failing at night
DNS failures
en.explanation: Per-tunnel QoS shapes each hub-to-spoke tunnel to the spoke's bandwidth; adaptive QoS adjusts the shaper to measured link capacity.

en.question: What does AppQoE TCP optimization do?
options: Proxies TCP to improve long-delay links
Converts all TCP sessions to UDP so that they can be sent faster
Blocks TCP retransmissions
Limits TCP to one session per user
en.explanation: TCP optimization terminates and re-originates TCP with better congestion control (BBR), helping high-latency or lossy paths.

en.question: How does DRE save WAN bandwidth?
options: Sends references instead of repeated data
Drops duplicate users from the network
Removes BFD packets from the tunnels
Turns off encryption to shrink the headers
en.explanation: Data Redundancy Elimination caches byte patterns at both ends and replaces repeated chunks with short signatures.

en.question: A voice site has two poor-quality links. Which AppQoE feature sends each packet over both?
options: Forward error correction using parity packets on a single link
Packet duplication
TCP optimization
DRE
en.explanation: Packet duplication sends copies over two tunnels and discards the duplicate at the far end, hiding loss on one path.

en.question: What does FEC do on a lossy tunnel?
options: Compresses the packet headers on the tunnel
Encrypts packets a second time with a new key
Moves the traffic to another TLOC colour
Adds parity to rebuild lost packets
en.explanation: Forward Error Correction sends a parity packet for each group so the receiver can recover a lost packet without retransmission.

en.question: What is AppNav in the AppQoE design?
options: The controller that redirects flows to service nodes
A GPS-based feature that maps every branch on a global map
A replacement for OMP in large hub sites
A GUI theme in the Manager dashboard
en.explanation: AppNav controllers intercept and distribute flows to service nodes (external or internal) that run TCP optimization and DRE.

en.question: How can SD-WAN Manager administrators be authenticated against a central server?
options: Using BFD keys
Only local accounts created on each edge router in VPN 512
RADIUS, TACACS+ or SSO
Using the device certificate serial
en.explanation: The Manager supports local users, RADIUS/TACACS+ and SAML SSO, with user groups for RBAC.

en.question: Where in SD-WAN Manager do you check tunnel loss, latency and jitter for a site?
options: Administration > Settings > Alarms
Configuration > Certificates for the edge and its controllers
Monitor > Devices > Tunnel / App Route
Maintenance > Software Repository
en.explanation: The device monitoring pages show tunnels, AAR statistics (app route), interfaces and events per device.

en.question: How does an external tool authenticate to the SD-WAN Manager REST API?
options: An SNMPv1 community string sent in every API request
Session cookie plus an XSRF token
A BFD key
No authentication is needed
en.explanation: A POST to j_security_check returns JSESSIONID; a GET to /dataservice/client/token returns the X-XSRF-TOKEN needed for changes (newer releases also support tokens).

en.question: How does SD-WAN Manager upgrade edge software safely?
options: Upload, activate, and auto-rollback if contact is lost
Copy the image to each edge by TFTP and reload them all at the same time
The Validator upgrades edges at random
Software cannot be upgraded from the Manager
en.explanation: Images go into the repository; devices install, then activate; if the device does not reach the Manager within the timer, it rolls back.

en.question: Which component automates and manages an SD-Access fabric?
options: Catalyst Center
Catalyst SD-WAN Validator in the cloud
Meraki dashboard
Prime Infrastructure 1.x
en.explanation: Catalyst Center (formerly DNA Center) provisions the underlay and overlay, policy and assurance; ISE provides identity and policy.

en.question: Which protocol is the control plane of an SD-Access fabric?
options: LISP
OSPF in a single area across all of the fabric nodes
OMP
VTP
en.explanation: LISP maps endpoint identifiers (EIDs) to routing locators (RLOCs); fabric nodes register and query the control plane node (map server/resolver). BGP EVPN is a newer option.

en.question: Which encapsulation forms the SD-Access data plane?
options: 802.1Q trunks only
IPsec in transport mode between every pair of nodes
MPLS
VXLAN
en.explanation: VXLAN-GPO carries the VN (VNI) and the scalable group tag (SGT) in its header between fabric nodes.

en.question: Which technology carries policy (who can talk to whom) in SD-Access?
options: Port numbers in the ACLs configured on each switch by hand
Cisco TrustSec SGTs
OSPF tags
DHCP option 82
en.explanation: SGTs are assigned by ISE at authentication, carried in VXLAN and enforced with SGACLs (group-based policy).

en.question: What is the recommended underlay design for SD-Access?
options: A hub-and-spoke GRE design to the core
A large layer 2 domain with spanning tree on every link
Only static routes between the switches
A routed layer 3 network, often IS-IS
en.explanation: The underlay is routed access with loopbacks reachable; LAN Automation builds an IS-IS underlay; manual OSPF/IS-IS also works.

en.question: What does LAN Automation in Catalyst Center do?
options: Upgrades the firmware of access points
Writes the SGACL matrix in ISE for every pair of groups
Discovers new switches and builds the underlay
Creates guest portals for visitors
en.explanation: Using a seed device and PnP, it onboards switches, assigns addressing and configures IS-IS and multicast for the underlay.

en.question: What is the role of a fabric edge node?
options: Runs ISE
Connects the fabric to the WAN and to the data centre via eBGP handoffs
Holds the host database only
Connects endpoints and registers them
en.explanation: Edge nodes are the access switches: they authenticate endpoints, register EIDs with the control plane node and encapsulate traffic.

en.question: What is the role of the control plane node?
options: The WLC for all the fabric APs
The device that hosts the anycast gateway for every endpoint on the floor
The host tracking database
The NTP server for the fabric nodes
en.explanation: It stores EID-to-RLOC mappings and answers queries from edge and border nodes; it is often collocated with the border.

en.question: What does a fabric border node do?
options: Authenticates every wired endpoint with 802.1X on its access ports
Connects the fabric to external networks
Hosts the Catalyst Center GUI
Assigns SGTs
en.explanation: Border nodes are the gateway between fabric and outside (internal or external borders), handing off VNs (often per VRF eBGP) and translating policy.

en.question: What is the anycast gateway in SD-Access?
options: The same gateway IP/MAC on every edge
A single router that all edge nodes forward to with a GRE tunnel
An HSRP pair running on the border nodes
A DHCP relay configured on ISE
en.explanation: Every edge node hosts the same SVI IP/MAC for a subnet, so endpoints can move anywhere without changing gateway.

en.question: What does ISE contribute to an SD-Access fabric?
options: The underlay routing protocol for all the switches in the fabric
Authentication and SGT assignment
VXLAN encapsulation on the edges
The map server for the fabric
en.explanation: ISE authenticates (802.1X/MAB), assigns VN/SGT, stores the group-based policy matrix and integrates with Catalyst Center via pxGrid/ERS.

en.question: Where are SGACLs typically enforced in SD-Access?
options: In Catalyst Center
At the ingress border of the internet provider before the firewall
On the WLC only
On the egress fabric edge
en.explanation: Policy is enforced at egress, where the destination SGT is known; the source SGT arrives in the VXLAN header.

en.question: How does SD-Access provide macro-segmentation?
options: SGTs inside a single routing table for the whole campus
Virtual networks
Port security on edge ports
Private VLANs on each switch
en.explanation: VNs are separate routing domains (VRFs); traffic between them must go through a fusion device or firewall. SGTs give micro-segmentation within a VN.

en.question: Two VNs (Employees and IoT) need some shared services such as DHCP and DNS. What is a common design?
options: Use the same SGT for both groups
Put DHCP and DNS servers in each VN as copies on every edge node
Merge both VNs into one single VN
A fusion device leaks routes
en.explanation: Shared services usually sit outside the fabric; a fusion device performs inter-VRF route leaking (or the border can do selective leaking).

en.question: How do wireless endpoints join an SD-Access fabric (fabric-enabled wireless)?
options: APs VXLAN client traffic to the edge
APs build CAPWAP tunnels carrying all data to the WLC in the DC
APs act as border nodes
APs do not support fabric
en.explanation: In fabric wireless, the WLC handles the control plane (CAPWAP) and registers clients in LISP, while data is VXLAN from the AP to the edge.

en.question: Where must fabric APs connect?
options: To the internet through a firewall
To any switch outside the fabric with a trunk to the WLC
Only to the border node of the site
Directly to fabric edge nodes
en.explanation: Fabric APs connect to edge nodes (or extended nodes) in the INFRA VN so they can build VXLAN tunnels to the edge.

en.question: What is an extended node in SD-Access?
options: A small switch extending the fabric
A switch that runs the full LISP control plane for the whole campus
A second Catalyst Center appliance
An ISE policy service node
en.explanation: Extended nodes (e.g. Catalyst IE or compact switches) connect to an edge via 802.1Q and let IoT/industrial devices join the fabric; policy is enforced on the edge.

en.question: Why does SD-Access use Layer 2 flooding only when enabled per pool?
options: To save licences
Because VXLAN cannot carry broadcast frames under any circumstances
Because ARP is not used
To reduce broadcast in the fabric
en.explanation: By default the fabric converts ARP to unicast using the control plane; Layer 2 flooding (via underlay multicast) is enabled only for apps that need broadcast.

en.question: In SD-Access, what is the difference between the underlay and the overlay?
options: They are two names for the same OSPF process
Underlay carries user traffic; overlay carries only management
Underlay is the routed network; overlay is the VXLAN VNs
The overlay is used only for wireless
en.explanation: The underlay provides RLOC reachability between nodes; overlays (VNs) run on top in VXLAN, independent of physical topology.

en.question: An endpoint roams from one edge node to another. How does the fabric update forwarding?
options: The DHCP server gives it a new IP
Spanning tree reconverges across the entire campus
The new edge registers the EID
The border floods ARP to all edges
en.explanation: The new edge registers the EID with the control plane node, which notifies the previous edge (away table), and remote nodes refresh via SMR.

en.question: What does Catalyst Center Assurance add to an SD-Access fabric?
options: Encryption of all the VXLAN traffic between the fabric nodes
Health scores and issues
Additional SGTs for each client
Underlay routing between nodes
en.explanation: Assurance collects telemetry and gives health of network, clients and apps, with guided remediation and path trace.

en.question: What is a fabric site?
options: An ISE deployment with two nodes
Only a single access switch that has been provisioned by LAN Automation
Any building that has Wi-Fi coverage
A fabric with its own control plane and border
en.explanation: A fabric site has its own edge, control plane and border nodes; several sites are interconnected with SD-Access transit.

en.question: What does Fabric in a Box (FiaB) mean?
options: Only a WLC embedded inside a switch
A pre-built rack that contains Catalyst Center, ISE and all of the switches
A virtual fabric hosted in the cloud
One switch as border, control plane and edge
en.explanation: FiaB suits small sites: a single switch (or stack) performs all three fabric roles, optionally with embedded wireless.

en.question: Which role does the WLC play in fabric wireless?
options: It forwards all wireless client data to the border in CAPWAP
Control plane for APs and clients, not data
It replaces the control plane node
None, WLC is not used
en.explanation: The fabric WLC manages APs and RF, authenticates clients and updates the control plane node with wireless client locations.

en.question: Why does SD-Access need the WLC and fabric APs to have low latency to the control plane?
options: Because the WLC replicates multicast
Because LISP only runs on links faster than 100 Gb/s
Fabric wireless needs about 20 ms RTT WLC to APs
Because ISE is in the WLC
en.explanation: Fabric mode wireless requires the WLC to be close to APs (typically RTT ≤20 ms) since client onboarding updates the fabric control plane in real time.

en.question: Which MTU consideration applies to the SD-Access underlay?
options: Keep 1500 everywhere; VXLAN adds nothing
Lower the MTU to 1400 on all client ports
Raise MTU (about 9100) for VXLAN overhead
Use a different MTU per virtual network
en.explanation: VXLAN adds 50 bytes; the underlay should use jumbo MTU so 1500-byte client frames are not fragmented. LAN Automation sets 9100.

en.question: Why should each fabric node have a /32 loopback advertised in the underlay?
options: It is required for DHCP option 43 on the APs
It is the anycast gateway used by every client
It is the node's RLOC for VXLAN
It replaces the management VLAN on access ports
en.explanation: The Loopback0 /32 is the routing locator; the underlay must carry host routes (no summarisation hiding RLOCs) for reachability tracking.

en.question: How many control plane nodes are recommended per fabric site for resilience?
options: One, since LISP cannot replicate its database
Two
Four, one per building in every case
One per edge node, collocated on each access switch
en.explanation: Two control plane nodes are deployed; edges register with both, so either can answer queries. Large sites may use more (up to six with LISP pub/sub).

en.question: What is the difference between an internal border and an external border?
options: Internal: known networks; external: default route out
Internal borders run on access switches; external borders run on the WLC
There is no difference in any release
External borders only connect wireless clients
en.explanation: Internal borders import specific prefixes (e.g. DC, shared services); external borders are the gateway of last resort (internet/unknown). An 'anywhere' border does both.

en.question: How does a border node usually hand off VNs to the fusion device?
options: GRE tunnels to the WLC for each VN
A single OSPF session that carries all VNs in the global table
A VRF-lite eBGP session per VN
Static routes only in the global table
en.explanation: Catalyst Center automates IP transit: a subinterface/SVI per VN with eBGP to the peer, which keeps VRF separation outside the fabric.

en.question: SGTs must be kept when traffic leaves the fabric through an IP transit. What can carry them?
options: The DSCP field of every packet, rewritten by the border
Inline tagging or SXP
The VLAN ID of the subinterface
They cannot leave the fabric at all
en.explanation: With IP transit the VXLAN header is removed; SGT can be kept with inline tagging (CMD) on the handoff or exchanged as IP-SGT mappings with SXP/pxGrid.

en.question: What is SD-Access transit used for?
options: Linking fabric sites while keeping VXLAN/SGT
Connecting the fabric to the internet provider with plain IP
Linking APs to the WLC across a WAN
Replacing ISE between sites
en.explanation: SD-Access transit (LISP pub/sub with transit control plane nodes) carries native VXLAN with VN and SGT end to end between sites, usually over a metro or campus core.

en.question: When is SD-WAN a better transit between fabric sites than SD-Access transit?
options: When no ISE is deployed anywhere
Sites in one building with dark fibre between them
When there are fewer than ten edge nodes
Sites connected over WAN links
en.explanation: Across a WAN, SD-WAN transit (integrated with Catalyst SD-WAN) carries VN and SGT over the SD-WAN overlay; SD-Access transit needs high bandwidth, low latency and jumbo MTU.

en.question: Which segmentation tool should separate employees from contractors in the same VN?
options: An extra MTU setting
A separate VN for every single user
A new fabric site for contractors
Different SGTs with an SGACL
en.explanation: Within a VN, micro-segmentation via SGTs and group-based policy is simpler than creating more VNs; VNs are for full isolation.

en.question: Why should the number of virtual networks be kept small?
options: Each VN adds VRFs, handoffs and route leaking
VNs cannot carry more than one SGT in any release
Each VN requires a separate Catalyst Center
VNs disable wireless
en.explanation: Every VN needs a VRF on all nodes, a border handoff and often fusion leaking; use VNs for strong isolation and SGTs for finer policy.

en.question: Which VN is used by default for fabric APs and extended nodes?
options: DEFAULT_VN, shared with all wired endpoints
INFRA_VN
GUEST_VN
A new VN per AP
en.explanation: INFRA_VN is in the global routing table and carries AP and extended node infrastructure; DEFAULT_VN is a user VN.

en.question: A site needs 40,000 endpoints. Which factor most limits the design?
options: Node host-table scale limits
The number of SSIDs on each AP
The MTU of client ports
The length of the VLAN names used
en.explanation: Scale depends on platform limits for host entries in the control plane, edge node host tables, VNs and SGACLs; large sites may need multiple sites or dedicated control plane nodes.

en.question: What is over-the-top (OTT) wireless in an SD-Access site?
options: A cloud-hosted WLC reached over the internet
APs that act as fabric edge nodes with VXLAN
CAPWAP carried over the fabric
Wireless clients without any SSID
en.explanation: OTT keeps the traditional centralized model: CAPWAP control and data pass over the fabric as normal traffic, without fabric policy for wireless clients.

en.question: When might OTT wireless be chosen over fabric wireless?
options: During migration or when the WLC is too far
When the site needs SGT policy for wireless clients
When the APs connect directly to edge nodes
When latency to the WLC is under 5 ms
en.explanation: OTT suits migration, unsupported AP/WLC models or high latency to the WLC; fabric wireless gives the same policy and mobility as wired.

en.question: What advantage does fabric wireless give compared with OTT?
options: Fewer access points needed on each floor
All traffic always passes through the WLC in the DC
No need for any WLC at all in the site
Same VN/SGT policy for wired and wireless
en.explanation: Wireless clients are registered in the fabric and their traffic is distributed at the edge, using the same segmentation and anycast gateway as wired.

en.question: How is multicast supported for overlay traffic in SD-Access?
options: Only through the WLC in the data centre
Multicast is converted to broadcast on all edge nodes
Head-end or native multicast
It is not supported in the overlay
en.explanation: Overlay multicast uses PIM in the VN with RPs; it is transported either by head-end replication (unicast copies) or native multicast in the underlay for efficiency.

en.question: Where is the rendezvous point (RP) for overlay multicast usually placed?
options: Inside the ISE PAN
On every client device
On the border nodes
On the AP
en.explanation: RPs for overlay PIM-SM are typically on borders (or external), possibly with anycast RP and MSDP for redundancy.

en.question: Which underlay feature is needed when native multicast or Layer 2 flooding is used?
options: Spanning tree on every routed link
PIM and multicast in the underlay
An SSID for each virtual network
802.1X on all routed uplinks
en.explanation: Native multicast and L2 flooding map overlay groups to underlay multicast groups, so the underlay needs PIM (often SSM or ASM with an RP).

en.question: A site has existing traditional switches that cannot become edge nodes. What can be used to migrate gradually?
options: Rip out all switches on the same night
A Layer 2 border handoff
Put old switches in INFRA_VN as edges
Enable VTP pruning
en.explanation: The L2 handoff on a border extends a fabric subnet to a traditional VLAN so hosts in both share the same subnet during migration.

en.question: Why is a dedicated, routed link between border nodes recommended?
options: It is needed for ISE to work with the borders
It carries the client DHCP traffic
Gives a path if one border loses uplinks
It replaces the control plane node
en.explanation: An iBGP/IGP link between the pair lets one border reach external networks via the other if its handoff fails, avoiding black holes.

en.question: Which port authentication template does Catalyst Center offer to keep endpoints working while 802.1X is introduced?
options: WPA3 on wired ports
Closed authentication with no fallback
No authentication on all ports forever
Open authentication (monitor mode)
en.explanation: Open/low-impact templates allow traffic while authenticating so failures are visible without outages; closed mode is applied later.

en.question: Where should the DHCP server be placed and what must the edge do for clients in the fabric?
options: Outside; the edge relays with option 82
On every edge node as a local DHCP server
Inside each access point on the floor
On the control plane node only
en.explanation: Edges relay DHCP (anycast gateway) and add option 82 with RLOC information so the reply can be returned to the right edge through the border.

en.question: Which policy model in Catalyst Center defines which groups can communicate?
options: Per-port ACLs typed on each switch
Group-based policy matrix
OSPF route maps on borders
SSID priority list on the WLC
en.explanation: The group-based policy matrix (source SGT × destination SGT) is authored in Catalyst Center and pushed to ISE, which downloads SGACLs to enforcing nodes.

en.question: Why is a default 'deny' between SGTs risky as a first step?
options: Unknown needed flows break
Because SGACLs cannot contain permit entries
Because ISE cannot push deny rules
Because VXLAN drops all denied traffic twice
en.explanation: A deny-by-default matrix requires knowing all required flows; most deployments start with permit plus logging/analytics, then tighten.

en.question: What should be checked before choosing switch models for SD-Access roles?
options: The compatibility matrix per role
Only the number of access ports
The colour of the chassis and its bezel
Whether the switch has a console port
en.explanation: Each release lists supported platforms and scale per role (edge, border, control plane, extended node) and supported WLC/AP models.

en.question: What does SD-Access stand for in Cisco campus networks?
options: Secure Data Access for WAN sites
Software-Defined Access
Switched Domain Access
Standard Distribution Access layer
en.explanation: SD-Access is Cisco's intent-based campus fabric, automated by Catalyst Center with ISE policy.

en.question: In LISP terms, what is an EID?
options: The IP address of the fabric node loopback
The endpoint's IP or MAC identity
The VXLAN header checksum
A Catalyst Center licence key
en.explanation: Endpoint Identifiers are host addresses; Routing Locators (RLOCs) are the fabric node addresses where those hosts sit.

en.question: In an SD-Access fabric, what does the routing locator (RLOC) refer to?
options: The SGT number assigned to a group
The MAC address of the endpoint itself
The node address behind which a host sits
The name of a virtual network
en.explanation: RLOCs are underlay addresses (usually Loopback0) used as VXLAN tunnel endpoints.

en.question: In SD-Access policy, what is an SGT and what does the acronym mean?
options: Security (scalable) Group Tag
Switch Gateway Table entry
Segment Group Tunnel identifier
Static Gateway Translation
en.explanation: A Security Group Tag (also called scalable group tag) is a 16-bit value identifying a group of users or devices.

en.question: Which VXLAN header field carries the SGT in SD-Access?
options: The VNI field
The outer IP TTL field of each packet
The UDP destination port
The Group Policy ID in VXLAN-GPO
en.explanation: VXLAN Group Policy Option adds a 16-bit Group Policy ID; the 24-bit VNI identifies the VN or L2 segment.

en.question: A wired user plugs in and authenticates with 802.1X. Which device tells the edge which VN and SGT to use?
options: The border node through an eBGP update
ISE, in the RADIUS authorisation
The control plane node
The DHCP server
en.explanation: ISE returns the VLAN/pool (mapped to a VN) and SGT in the authorisation result; the edge then registers the endpoint.

en.question: An edge node needs to send traffic to an unknown destination outside the fabric. Where does it send it?
options: To all edge nodes as a broadcast frame
To the external border
Back to the source edge node
To the WLC for the floor
en.explanation: If the control plane has no mapping, the edge uses the external border as the default (proxy) to reach networks outside the fabric.

en.question: Which Catalyst Center workflow assigns IP pools to VNs at a site?
options: Assurance health dashboard
Software image management for switches
Host onboarding / VN-to-pool mapping
Backup and restore
en.explanation: In Provision > Fabric Sites, host onboarding binds IP pools to VNs, sets authentication templates and assigns ports.

en.question: Why is pxGrid integration between Catalyst Center and ISE important?
options: Shares groups, policy and context
It is the transport for VXLAN data
It runs the LISP map server
It assigns IP addresses
en.explanation: Catalyst Center uses ERS/pxGrid to read and write SGTs, policies and endpoint context in ISE, keeping one source of truth.

en.question: Two fabric sites share a subnet for a legacy app across a campus core with jumbo MTU. Which transit preserves VN and SGT?
options: SD-Access transit
IP transit with static routes only
SD-WAN transit through the internet
No transit is possible
en.explanation: SD-Access transit keeps native VXLAN with VN and SGT between sites over a high-performance core.

en.question: What is a common place for a firewall in an SD-Access design for inter-VN traffic?
options: Between the edge and the client
Inside each access point radio
On the control plane node only
Beyond the border as the fusion device
en.explanation: A firewall acting as fusion (or behind the border) inspects traffic between VNs and to shared services or the internet.

en.question: Why are critical VLANs/pools configured on edge ports?
options: To disable 802.1X permanently
To give guests faster Wi-Fi
To allow spanning tree on edge ports
Access continues if ISE is down
en.explanation: If RADIUS servers are unreachable, critical authorisation puts endpoints in a defined pool/VN so business continues.

en.question: Silent hosts (e.g. printers that never send traffic first) cause reachability issues. Which feature helps?
options: Removing the anycast gateway
Lowering the underlay MTU
L2 flooding in that pool
Disabling LISP on the edge nodes
en.explanation: Because the fabric learns hosts when they talk, silent hosts may be unknown; L2 flooding lets ARP reach them (or static/known registration).

en.question: Where should Catalyst Center and ISE be placed relative to fabric sites?
options: Inside every fabric edge as containers
In a shared services block
On the access points of each floor
Only in the public internet
en.explanation: They are management/policy components reached via the underlay or a border; they are not part of the fabric data path.

en.question: Catalyst Center is unreachable for a day. What happens to an operating SD-Access fabric?
options: Traffic keeps flowing; changes stop
All VXLAN tunnels go down at once
Clients lose their SGTs and their VN
The underlay stops routing between nodes
en.explanation: Catalyst Center is the management plane; the control, data and policy planes keep running on the nodes and ISE.

en.question: Which access-layer switch design best suits SD-Access edge redundancy for endpoints?
options: Wireless mesh only between floors
A single switch with one uplink
Daisy-chained hubs on each floor
Stacks with dual uplinks
en.explanation: Endpoints attach to one edge; stacks (or StackWise Virtual at distribution) plus routed dual uplinks give resilience.

en.question: A distribution switch between edges and borders runs no fabric features. Which statement describes it?
options: A node that terminates CAPWAP
A node that holds the LISP database
An intermediate node routing only underlay
A node that runs ISE for the fabric
en.explanation: Intermediate nodes (e.g. distribution/core) only route underlay traffic; they do not encapsulate VXLAN or need fabric features.

en.question: A guest VN must use a separate internet path. What design is typical?
options: A separate SSID with no VN mapping
Guest users in the same VN as employees
Guest VN handed off to a guest firewall
Guests routed via the control plane
en.explanation: The guest VN is handed off at the border (or dedicated guest border/control plane) to a DMZ firewall for isolated internet access.

en.question: Which protocol can optionally replace LISP as the SD-Access control plane in newer releases?
options: RIPv2 with authentication
BGP EVPN
HSRP version 2
VTP version 3
en.explanation: Recent Catalyst Center releases support a BGP EVPN-based fabric option alongside the classic LISP control plane.

en.question: What does an SGACL contain?
options: Rules between two groups
A list of VLANs per access port
The map of RLOC addresses
Routing table entries for the VN
en.explanation: An SGACL is an ACL (e.g. permit tcp 443, deny ip) applied to traffic from a source SGT to a destination SGT.

pt.question: Nos switches Nexus, que comando tem de ser introduzido antes de se poder configurar OSPF?
options: feature ospf
router ospf enable-all
ip routing ospf
install license ospf
pt.explanation: O NX-OS é modular: as features (ospf, bgp, pim, vpc, lacp, interface-vlan…) têm de ser ativadas antes de os seus comandos aparecerem.

pt.question: Numa fabric VXLAN EVPN, para que se usa o MP-BGP?
options: Eleger a root bridge do spanning tree
Criar a adjacência do underlay só em cada ligação física
Levar rotas MAC/IP de anfitriões na família EVPN
Sincronizar as tabelas MAC dos pares vPC
pt.explanation: O MP-BGP L2VPN EVPN anuncia rotas MAC/IP de anfitriões (tipo 2) e de prefixos (tipo 5) entre VTEP, normalmente com os spines como route reflectors.

pt.question: Que modo PIM se usa normalmente no underlay VXLAN flood-and-learn ou EVPN para tráfego BUM?
options: Sem multicast; o BUM é sempre descartado
PIM dense mode a inundar todas as interfaces
PIM sparse mode com anycast RP nos spines
PIM nas portas de acesso para os servidores
pt.explanation: A replicação multicast do BUM usa PIM-SM (ou bidir) no underlay, com anycast RP nos spines; a replicação na entrada é a alternativa.

pt.question: Dois switches Nexus num par vPC correm HSRP. Como é tratado o tráfego para o MAC virtual?
options: A peer link do vPC leva-o todo
Só o par HSRP ativo encaminha, o outro descarta
Os dois pares encaminham-no (ativo-ativo)
O HSRP não é suportado com vPC
pt.explanation: Com vPC, o standby também encaminha os pacotes enviados para o vMAC HSRP, por isso os dois pares encaminham e a peer link não é usada para isso.

pt.question: Que elemento do vPC leva as mensagens de heartbeat para detetar uma situação dual-active?
options: A própria peer link do vPC
A ligação peer-keepalive
O port channel membro para o anfitrião
A ACL da VRF de gestão
pt.explanation: O peer-keepalive (muitas vezes pela mgmt0) verifica se o par está vivo; a peer link leva o controlo (CFS) e algum tráfego de dados.

pt.question: A peer link do vPC falha mas o keepalive continua ativo. O que faz o par secundário?
options: Suspende as suas portas membro vPC
Passa a primário e mantém todas as portas vPC ativas
Reinicia para voltar a entrar no domínio
Desliga a ligação keepalive
pt.explanation: Para evitar split brain, o secundário suspende as suas portas membro vPC (e SVI) enquanto o primário continua a encaminhar.

pt.question: O que dá o Rapid PVST+ em relação ao PVST+ clássico?
options: Uma única árvore para todas as VLAN da fabric
Convergência mais rápida com RSTP por VLAN
Encaminhamento camada 3 entre VLAN
Negociação LACP automática
pt.explanation: O Rapid PVST+ corre uma instância 802.1w por VLAN, com proposal/agreement para convergência abaixo do segundo em ligações ponto a ponto.

pt.question: Que modo LACP nos dois lados faz com que não se forme port channel?
options: on / on
active / active
active / passive (with rate fast)
passive / passive
pt.explanation: Pelo menos um lado tem de estar em active para enviar LACPDU; passive-passive nunca negoceia. O 'on' é estático e não usa LACP.

pt.question: O que faz um VTEP numa fabric VXLAN?
options: Encapsula e desencapsula tráfego VXLAN
Corre a eleição da root do spanning tree
Atribui VSAN às portas Fibre Channel
Guarda a base de dados de configuração do APIC
pt.explanation: Os VXLAN Tunnel Endpoints (interfaces NVE dos leafs) mapeiam VLAN para VNI e acrescentam os cabeçalhos UDP/IP exteriores para os VTEP remotos.

pt.question: Em VXLAN EVPN, o que dá o distributed anycast gateway?
options: Um router central para todas as sub-redes
O mesmo gateway em todos os leafs
HSRP entre dois spines
Um gateway só nos border leafs
pt.explanation: Cada leaf é o gateway de primeiro salto dos anfitriões locais com o mesmo anycast MAC (fabric forwarding), dando encaminhamento ótimo e mobilidade.

pt.question: Que tipo de rota EVPN anuncia prefixos IP (p. ex. rotas externas) para a fabric?
options: Tipo 4
Tipo 2
Tipo 3
Tipo 5
pt.explanation: O tipo 2 leva MAC/IP de anfitriões, o tipo 3 multicast inclusivo (BUM), o tipo 4 o segmento Ethernet, o tipo 5 rotas de prefixos IP.

pt.question: Porque se usa ARP suppression em VXLAN EVPN?
options: Passa o processamento ARP para os spines
Bloqueia todo o ARP para travar ataques de spoofing
Substitui o endereçamento IP por encaminhamento só por MAC
O leaf responde ao ARP com dados EVPN
pt.explanation: Com as associações MAC/IP aprendidas pelas rotas tipo 2, o leaf local responde aos pedidos ARP em vez de os inundar pela fabric.

pt.question: Como descobre uma fabric ACI novos switches leaf e spine?
options: Através do vCenter
CLI manual em cada switch com IP estático
DHCP a partir do router WAN
Descoberta por LLDP e registo no APIC
pt.explanation: Os switches são encontrados por LLDP e DHCP a partir do APIC (VLAN infra/pool TEP); o administrador regista-os com IDs e nomes de nó.

pt.question: Nas access policies do ACI, que objeto liga uma VLAN pool a um domínio?
options: O subject do contrato
A sub-rede do bridge domain
O domínio
A VRF do tenant
pt.explanation: Os domínios referem VLAN pools e ligam-se a AAEP; os AAEP associam-se a interface policy groups para as VLAN serem permitidas nas portas.

pt.question: Uma static port binding de uma EPG falha com uma falha de 'VLAN inválida'. Qual é uma causa provável?
options: A VLAN falta na VLAN pool
O bridge domain não tem sub-rede
O contrato não tem filtro
A VRF está em modo unenforced
pt.explanation: A cadeia interface → policy group → AAEP → domínio → VLAN pool tem de incluir a VLAN, e a EPG tem de estar associada a esse domínio.

pt.question: O que faz a integração VMM do ACI com o vCenter?
options: Mapeia EPG para port groups num VDS
Move máquinas virtuais entre anfitriões automaticamente
Instala o ESXi nos switches leaf
Faz cópia da base de dados do vCenter para o APIC
pt.explanation: O APIC cria um VDS no vCenter; cada EPG associada ao domínio VMM aparece como port group, com atribuição dinâmica de VLAN.

pt.question: No ACI, um leaf recebe um pacote para um IP de destino desconhecido na mesma VRF. Para onde é enviado por omissão?
options: Para o proxy dos spines
Inundado para todos os leafs da fabric
Descartado de imediato no leaf
Para o APIC fazer a consulta
pt.explanation: Os leafs enviam o unicast desconhecido para o TEP de proxy anycast dos spines; os spines têm a base de dados COOP e encaminham para o leaf certo.

pt.question: No modelo de cloud do NIST, que modelo de serviço dá ao cliente máquinas virtuais, gerindo ele o sistema operativo?
options: PaaS
SaaS
IaaS
Só FaaS
pt.explanation: O IaaS fornece computação, armazenamento e rede; o cliente gere o SO e as aplicações. O PaaS acrescenta o runtime; o SaaS entrega a aplicação completa.

pt.question: Que modelo de implementação do NIST é usado em exclusivo por uma organização, no local ou fora?
options: Cloud privada
Cloud pública
Cloud comunitária
Cloud híbrida
pt.explanation: A cloud privada é de uma organização; a comunitária é partilhada por organizações com interesses comuns; a híbrida combina duas ou mais.

pt.question: Que funcionalidade do NX-OS permite atualizar um switch Nexus com o mínimo de interrupção do plano de dados?
options: Apagar a configuração de arranque
ISSU
Reiniciar para o prompt do loader
Substituir primeiro a supervisora
pt.explanation: O ISSU atualiza o plano de controlo enquanto o plano de dados continua a encaminhar (em plataformas/caminhos suportados); verifique antes a compatibilidade.

pt.question: O que é o EPLD num switch Nexus?
options: Uma licença para portas extra no chassis
Um protocolo de encaminhamento para ligações de centro de dados
Lógica de hardware atualizada à parte
O processo de eleição do primário vPC
pt.explanation: Os Electronic Programmable Logic Devices têm funções de hardware; as imagens EPLD atualizam-se à parte e normalmente exigem reinício.

pt.question: Como se aplicam correções individuais no NX-OS sem atualização completa?
options: Editando só a configuração em uso
Voltando à versão anterior
Patches SMU
Reinstalando a BIOS do switch
pt.explanation: Os SMU instalam-se com 'install add / activate / commit' para corrigir defeitos específicos da versão em uso.

pt.question: Que funcionalidade do NX-OS permite voltar a um instantâneo de configuração anterior?
options: write erase and reload the switch
copy startup-config tftp
Checkpoint e rollback
reload in 10 with save
pt.explanation: O 'checkpoint' guarda a configuração em uso; 'rollback running-config checkpoint NOME' repõe-na (atomic, best-effort ou stop-at-first-failure).

pt.question: Que funcionalidade copia tráfego de portas de origem para uma porta de destino de um analisador?
options: CFS
NetFlow
LLDP
SPAN
pt.explanation: O SPAN espelha pacotes (o ERSPAN envia-os por GRE para um analisador remoto); o NetFlow exporta registos de fluxos, não pacotes.

pt.question: Qual é uma vantagem da telemetria em streaming baseada em modelos face à consulta SNMP?
options: Não precisa de nenhum coletor externo
Usa menos modelos YANG por equipamento
Só funciona em ligações série antigas
Os equipamentos enviam os dados
pt.explanation: A telemetria envia dados estruturados (gRPC/gNMI, caminhos YANG) periodicamente ou por mudança, em escala e com pouca latência.

pt.question: O que oferece o Nexus Dashboard para um centro de dados?
options: Só uma ferramenta de zoning Fibre Channel
Só um gestor de chassis de servidores blade
Uma plataforma de serviços para fabrics
Um substituto do NX-OS
pt.explanation: O Nexus Dashboard aloja serviços como Fabric Controller, Insights e Orchestrator para gerir e analisar fabrics NX-OS e ACI.

pt.question: Como podem ser geridos os servidores rack Cisco UCS C-Series?
options: CIMC, Intersight ou UCSM
Só pela interface do APIC da fabric
Só por cabo de consola série
Através das peer links do vPC
pt.explanation: O CIMC dá gestão standalone; os servidores também se podem ligar a Fabric Interconnects (UCSM ou Intersight Managed Mode) ou ao Intersight standalone.

pt.question: Porque usar pools de MAC, WWN e UUID nos service profiles UCS?
options: As identidades seguem o perfil
Aceleram o CPU e a memória
Substituem as VLAN na fabric
Licenciam o servidor no UCS Manager
pt.explanation: Computação sem estado: as identidades vêm de pools do perfil, por isso um perfil pode passar para outra blade sem mudar a configuração a montante.

pt.question: Qual é a diferença entre um template de service profile initial e um updating no UCS Manager?
options: Os initial atualizam os perfis em cada alteração
Os updating propagam as alterações
São idênticos em todas as versões
Os updating não podem usar pools
pt.explanation: Os perfis de um template updating ficam ligados e herdam as alterações (que podem reiniciar servidores); os initial só criam os perfis uma vez.

pt.question: No UCS, o que é um vHBA?
options: Uma definição do controlador RAID
Uma NIC Ethernet virtual com um MAC
Um controlador de armazenamento do hipervisor
Um adaptador FC virtual com um WWPN
pt.explanation: Os vHBA definem-se no service profile, recebem WWNN/WWPN de pools e ligam-se às VSAN através dos Fabric Interconnects.

pt.question: Uma blade UCS tem de arrancar de um LUN da SAN. O que é preciso no service profile?
options: Uma boot policy com alvos SAN
Uma local disk policy com qualquer configuração
Uma BIOS policy que desliga a virtualização
Uma lista de vNIC vazia
pt.explanation: A boot policy indica o vHBA e o WWPN/LUN do alvo; o zoning e o LUN masking no armazenamento têm de permitir o iniciador.

pt.question: O que é o Intersight Managed Mode (IMM) para UCS X-Series?
options: Gerir servidores só pelo CIMC local
O Intersight a gerir FI e servidores
Um modo ACI para os switches leaf
Um modo de firmware de arrays de armazenamento
pt.explanation: No IMM, o Intersight gere FI, chassis e servidores com pools, políticas e server profiles; o UCS X-Series exige-o (sem UCSM).

pt.question: O que garante um host firmware package no UCS?
options: Criação automática de VLAN nos uplinks
Velocidades de DIMM maiores
Versões de firmware consistentes
Ativação de licenças para cada blade
pt.explanation: Os firmware packages (ou as políticas de firmware do Intersight) definem as versões de BIOS, adaptador e controlador aplicadas ao associar o perfil.

pt.question: Que tipo de cópia de segurança do UCS Manager pode repor todo o sistema num par de Fabric Interconnects substituído?
options: Ficheiro de tech-support
Só exportação da configuração lógica
Exportação do registo de eventos
Full state backup
pt.explanation: O full state é um instantâneo binário para recuperação de desastres; as exportações all-configuration, logical e system são XML para importar definições.

pt.question: Como pode capturar tráfego da vNIC de um servidor UCS para análise?
options: Exportar um full state backup
Ativar registo de debug na BIOS
Usar a consola KVM do servidor
Uma sessão de traffic monitoring no FI
pt.explanation: As sessões de traffic monitoring do UCS Manager espelham o tráfego de vNIC/vHBA ou de uplinks para uma porta de destino no FI.

pt.question: O que é uma VSAN nos switches Cisco MDS e Nexus?
options: Um domínio vPC para portas de armazenamento
Uma VLAN que leva só tráfego iSCSI
Um volume de um array de discos
Uma fabric SAN virtual
pt.explanation: As VSAN isolam fabrics Fibre Channel no mesmo hardware; cada uma corre os seus serviços (FSPF, zoning, servidor de nomes).

pt.question: Durante a inicialização de uma fabric Fibre Channel, o que faz o principal switch?
options: Guarda os dados de todos os membros de zonas
Atribui domain IDs aos switches
Cifra todas as tramas FC
Elege o primário do vPC
pt.explanation: A seleção do principal switch faz-se por VSAN; atribui domain IDs, que formam o primeiro byte de cada FCID.

pt.question: Quais são as três partes de um FCID?
options: VSAN, VLAN e porta
Domínio, área e porta
WWNN, WWPN e LUN
Local, bastidor e ranhura
pt.explanation: O FCID de 24 bits é domínio (switch), área e porta; é atribuído no login na fabric (FLOGI).

pt.question: Para que serve o zoning numa SAN Fibre Channel?
options: Atribuir FCID aos anfitriões
Limitar que iniciadores veem que alvos
Agregar ISL num port channel
Definir o MTU dos uplinks da VSAN
pt.explanation: As zonas (normalmente um iniciador e um alvo, ou smart zoning) limitam a comunicação; os zonesets ativam-se por VSAN.

pt.question: O que acrescenta o enhanced zoning em relação ao basic zoning?
options: Um bloqueio de alterações na fabric
Zonas que abrangem várias VSAN
Cifra dos membros das zonas
LUN masking automático nos arrays
pt.explanation: O enhanced zoning usa um bloqueio de sessão para só um administrador editar de cada vez e depois aplica de forma atómica; o basic pode sobrepor alterações.

pt.question: Que comando mostra os equipamentos registados no servidor de nomes Fibre Channel?
options: show zone active
show flogi interface status
show fcns database
show vsan membership
pt.explanation: A base de dados FCNS lista FCID, WWPN e tipos FC4 da VSAN; o 'show flogi database' lista os logins locais.

pt.question: Porque usar device aliases numa fabric MDS?
options: Substituir as zonas por VSAN
Encaminhamento mais rápido das tramas FC
Mais buffer credits em cada ISL
Nomes para WWPN, partilhados por CFS
pt.explanation: Os device aliases ligam nomes a pWWN e são distribuídos por toda a fabric via CFS, para as zonas serem legíveis e fáceis de atualizar quando as HBA mudam.

pt.question: O que faz o modo NPV num Fabric Interconnect UCS ou num switch Nexus?
options: Bloqueia todos os FLOGI dos anfitriões
Transforma o switch num switch FC completo
Passa os logins dos hosts ao core
Corre FSPF até ao core
pt.explanation: Em NPV o switch de periferia passa os FLOGI como FDISC a um core com NPIV, evitando gastar domain IDs e problemas de interoperabilidade.

pt.question: O que tem de estar ativo no switch core para os switches de periferia em NPV se ligarem?
options: feature lacp
feature npv
só feature fport-channel-trunk
feature npiv
pt.explanation: O NPIV deixa uma porta F aceitar vários logins de portas N (FDISC); o core precisa de NPIV enquanto a periferia corre NPV.

pt.question: Porque agregar ISL entre dois switches MDS num SAN port channel?
options: Mais largura de banda e resiliência
Para juntar duas VSAN numa
Para desligar o zoning entre os switches
Para atribuir novos domain IDs
pt.explanation: Um SAN port channel aparece como um único ISL lógico: o tráfego é balanceado e a falha de um membro não provoca reconvergência FSPF.

pt.question: O que faz o CFS nos switches MDS e Nexus?
options: Comprime as tramas FC em ligações longas
Partilha configuração entre switches
Cria VSAN automaticamente
Monitoriza as ventoinhas do chassis
pt.explanation: O Cisco Fabric Services distribui e bloqueia configuração (device alias, NTP, port security, etc.) por toda a fabric.

pt.question: Que protocolo leva comandos SCSI por uma rede TCP/IP normal?
options: iSCSI
FCoE
NFS
FSPF
pt.explanation: O iSCSI usa TCP 3260; o FCoE leva tramas FC diretamente sobre Ethernet sem perdas; o NFS é armazenamento ao nível de ficheiros.

pt.question: Qual é a diferença principal entre armazenamento NFS e iSCSI?
options: O NFS precisa de switches Fibre Channel
O NFS é ficheiro; o iSCSI é bloco
O iSCSI só corre em InfiniBand
São o mesmo protocolo
pt.explanation: O NFS é um sistema de ficheiros de rede (NAS); o iSCSI dá ao anfitrião um dispositivo de blocos que ele próprio formata.

pt.question: O que se deve verificar antes de uma atualização de software sem interrupção num MDS?
options: Que todas as zonas estão desativadas
A saída do 'show install all impact'
Que todos os ISL estão desligados
Que a base de dados FCNS foi limpa
pt.explanation: O 'show install all impact' indica se os módulos atualizam sem impacto; supervisoras duplas e versões compatíveis permitem atualizar sem interrupção.

pt.question: Que funcionalidade do MDS analisa o desempenho de I/O SCSI/NVMe por fluxo?
options: SAN Analytics
Port security
Device alias
Zone merge
pt.explanation: O SAN Analytics (com o SAN Insights no Nexus Dashboard) inspeciona tramas em módulos suportados e mostra latência, IOPS e erros por iniciador-alvo-LUN.

pt.question: O que faz o Embedded Event Manager (EEM) no NX-OS?
options: Balanceia tráfego pelos ISL
Atualiza o software todas as semanas
Executa ações em eventos definidos
Sincroniza a configuração vPC com o par
pt.explanation: Os applets EEM identificam eventos (syslog, contadores, CLI) e executam ações como comandos CLI ou scripts.

pt.question: Que funcionalidade do NX-OS corre tarefas (como cópias da configuração) a horas definidas?
options: EEM tracking
Scheduler
Checkpoint
POAP
pt.explanation: A feature scheduler define jobs e horários (p. ex. copiar todos os dias a running-config para um servidor).

pt.question: Qual é a diferença entre a Bash shell e a Guest Shell no NX-OS?
options: São o mesmo ambiente com outros nomes
A Guest Shell é um contentor isolado
A Guest Shell precisa de servidor externo
A Bash só corre scripts Python 2
pt.explanation: A Bash dá acesso Linux nativo ao switch; a Guest Shell é um contentor LXC baseado em CentOS para correr aplicações e Python com segurança.

pt.question: O que permite o NX-API CLI a um script?
options: Ler traps SNMP do switch
Substituir o NX-OS por Linux
Configurar só as definições da BIOS
Enviar CLI por HTTPS e receber JSON
pt.explanation: O NX-API (feature nxapi) aceita pedidos JSON-RPC/ins_api com comandos show ou config e devolve saída estruturada.

pt.question: O Python no próprio equipamento NX-OS usa que módulo para correr comandos CLI?
options: requests
netmiko
paramiko
cli
pt.explanation: O módulo cli local dá cli(), clid() (JSON) e clip(); ferramentas externas como o netmiko usam SSH.

pt.question: Porque é o Ansible popular na automação de redes de centro de dados?
options: Precisa de um agente em cada switch
Não usa agentes e usa playbooks YAML
Só funciona com servidores UCS
Compila os playbooks para firmware
pt.explanation: O Ansible liga-se aos equipamentos com network_cli ou httpapi (p. ex. coleções cisco.nxos, cisco.aci), usando módulos idempotentes.

pt.question: O que faz o POAP num switch Nexus novo?
options: Cria uma peer link vPC com o vizinho
Entra automaticamente numa fabric ACI
Usa DHCP para obter imagem e config
Corre o Terraform a partir da bootflash
pt.explanation: O Power-On Auto Provisioning usa opções DHCP para encontrar um servidor de scripts, e depois o script obtém a imagem e a configuração.

pt.question: O que faz o passo 'plan' do Terraform com o provider ACI?
options: Faz primeiro cópia do APIC
Aplica todas as alterações de uma vez
Apaga e recria o tenant
Mostra as alterações previstas
pt.explanation: O terraform plan compara o estado pretendido com o estado/objetos reais; depois o apply cria, altera ou destrói recursos.

pt.question: Que interfaces permitem automatizar o Cisco Intersight?
options: Só pedidos SNMP get
Só a interface web
API REST, SDK e Terraform
Só a consola série de cada servidor
pt.explanation: O Intersight expõe uma interface REST OpenAPI com chaves de API, SDK, um provider Terraform e módulos Ansible.

pt.question: Porque precisam os clusters de treino de IA/ML de funcionalidades Ethernet sem perdas como PFC e ECN?
options: O tráfego RoCEv2 sofre com perdas
As GPU só usam Fibre Channel
Precisam de spanning tree em todas as ligações
Para reduzir a tabela MAC dos leafs
pt.explanation: O RDMA over Converged Ethernet espera não haver perdas; o PFC pausa por prioridade e o ECN/DCQCN sinaliza congestionamento antes das perdas.

pt.question: Que protocolo é preferido no AAA de administração de equipamentos por poder autorizar cada comando?
options: TACACS+
RADIUS
LDAP
SNMPv2c
pt.explanation: O TACACS+ separa autenticação, autorização e contabilização e suporta autorização por comando.

pt.question: No ACI, o que tem de existir para duas EPG comunicarem?
options: Um contrato entre elas
Um ID de VLAN partilhado
A mesma sub-rede IP
Uma rota estática
pt.explanation: O ACI funciona por lista branca: uma EPG fornece e outra consome um contrato cujos subjects e filtros permitem o tráfego.

pt.question: O que permite a microssegmentação (uSeg EPG) no ACI?
options: Cifrar toda a fabric
Dividir um leaf em dois switches
Agrupar endpoints por atributos
Criar VSAN para as VM
pt.explanation: As uSeg EPG classificam endpoints por atributos (IP, MAC, nome da VM, SO…) para a política se aplicar mesmo dentro do mesmo BD/port group.

pt.question: Que funcionalidade de first-hop security bloqueia servidores DHCP falsos nas portas de acesso?
options: Storm control
DHCP snooping
BPDU guard
UDLD
pt.explanation: O DHCP snooping só confia nas portas de uplink para mensagens de servidor e cria a tabela de associações usada pelo DAI e pelo IP Source Guard.

pt.question: Porque configurar uma keychain nos protocolos de encaminhamento do NX-OS?
options: Para acelerar a convergência
Para cifrar dados dos utilizadores
Para guardar passwords locais
Para rodar chaves de autenticação
pt.explanation: As keychains têm várias chaves com validades de envio/aceitação, permitindo trocar sem impacto a autenticação de OSPF, EIGRP, BGP ou HSRP.

pt.question: O que dá o MACsec numa ligação entre dois switches Nexus?
options: Túneis IPsec de ponta a ponta
Cifra da ligação na camada 2
Proteção de DHCP na ligação
Negociação LACP mais rápida
pt.explanation: O MACsec (802.1AE) cifra as tramas em cada ligação à velocidade da linha, com chaves do MKA (chave pré-partilhada ou 802.1X).

pt.question: O que faz o port security num switch MDS?
options: Cria zonas automaticamente
Cifra todas as tramas FC
Limita a largura de banda dos ISL
Liga WWN a portas
pt.explanation: O port security restringe que equipamentos (pWWN/nWWN/sWWN) podem fazer login em que interfaces; os logins indevidos são rejeitados.

pt.question: Em que difere o fabric binding do port security no MDS?
options: Cifra o tráfego dos ISL
Controla os anfitriões nas portas F
Controla que switches entram
Substitui o zoning da VSAN
pt.explanation: O fabric binding autoriza os WWN (e domain IDs) de switches em portas E/TE, impedindo switches não autorizados de se juntarem à fabric.

en.question: On Nexus switches, which command must be entered before OSPF can be configured?
options: feature ospf
router ospf enable-all
ip routing ospf
install license ospf
en.explanation: NX-OS is modular: features (ospf, bgp, pim, vpc, lacp, interface-vlan…) must be enabled before their commands appear.

en.question: In a VXLAN EVPN fabric, what is MP-BGP used for?
options: Electing the spanning tree root bridge
Building the underlay adjacency on every physical link only
Carrying MAC/IP host routes in the EVPN family
Synchronising vPC peer MAC tables
en.explanation: MP-BGP L2VPN EVPN advertises host MAC/IP (type-2) and prefix (type-5) routes between VTEPs, usually with spines as route reflectors.

en.question: Which PIM mode is commonly used in a VXLAN flood-and-learn or EVPN underlay for BUM traffic?
options: No multicast; BUM is always dropped
PIM dense mode flooding to every interface
PIM sparse mode with anycast RP on spines
PIM on access ports toward servers
en.explanation: Multicast replication for BUM uses PIM-SM (or bidir) in the underlay, with anycast RPs on spines; ingress replication is the alternative.

en.question: Two Nexus switches in a vPC pair run HSRP. How is traffic to the virtual MAC handled?
options: The vPC peer link carries all of it
Only the HSRP active peer forwards, the other drops it
Both peers forward it (active-active)
HSRP is not supported with vPC
en.explanation: With vPC, the standby also routes packets sent to the HSRP vMAC, so both peers forward and the peer link is not used for it.

en.question: Which vPC element carries heartbeat messages to detect a dual-active condition?
options: The vPC peer link itself
The peer-keepalive link
The member port channel to the host
The management VRF ACL
en.explanation: Peer-keepalive (often over mgmt0) checks that the peer is alive; the peer link carries control (CFS) and some data traffic.

en.question: The vPC peer link fails while the keepalive is still up. What does the secondary peer do?
options: Suspends its vPC member ports
Becomes primary and keeps all vPC ports up
Reboots to rejoin the domain
Disables the keepalive link
en.explanation: To avoid split brain, the secondary suspends its vPC member ports (and SVIs) while the primary keeps forwarding.

en.question: What does Rapid PVST+ provide compared with classic PVST+?
options: A single tree for all VLANs in the fabric
Faster convergence using RSTP per VLAN
Layer 3 routing between VLANs
Automatic LACP negotiation
en.explanation: Rapid PVST+ runs an 802.1w instance per VLAN, with proposal/agreement for sub-second convergence on point-to-point links.

en.question: Which LACP mode on both sides results in no port channel forming?
options: on / on
active / active
active / passive (with rate fast)
passive / passive
en.explanation: At least one side must be active to send LACPDUs; passive-passive never negotiates. 'on' is static and does not use LACP.

en.question: What does a VTEP do in a VXLAN fabric?
options: Encapsulates and decapsulates VXLAN
Runs the spanning tree root election
Assigns VSANs to Fibre Channel ports
Stores the APIC configuration database
en.explanation: VXLAN Tunnel Endpoints (leaf NVE interfaces) map VLANs to VNIs and add the outer UDP/IP headers toward remote VTEPs.

en.question: In VXLAN EVPN, what does distributed anycast gateway provide?
options: One central router for all subnets
The same gateway on every leaf
HSRP between two spines
A gateway only on border leafs
en.explanation: Each leaf is the first-hop gateway for its local hosts with the same anycast MAC (fabric forwarding), giving optimal routing and mobility.

en.question: Which EVPN route type advertises IP prefixes (e.g. external routes) into the fabric?
options: Type 4
Type 2
Type 3
Type 5
en.explanation: Type-2 carries MAC/IP of hosts, type-3 inclusive multicast (BUM), type-4 Ethernet segment, type-5 IP prefix routes.

en.question: Why is ARP suppression used in VXLAN EVPN?
options: It moves ARP processing to the spines
It blocks all ARP to stop spoofing attacks
It replaces IP addressing with MAC-only forwarding
Leafs answer ARP from EVPN data, cutting flooding
en.explanation: With learned MAC/IP bindings from type-2 routes, the local leaf replies to ARP requests instead of flooding them across the fabric.

en.question: How does an ACI fabric discover new leaf and spine switches?
options: Through vCenter host profiles
Manual CLI on every switch with a static IP
DHCP from the WAN router in the campus
LLDP discovery and APIC registration
en.explanation: Switches are found via LLDP and DHCP from the APIC (infra VLAN/TEP pool); the admin registers them with node IDs and names.

en.question: In ACI access policies, which object ties a VLAN pool to a domain?
options: The contract subject
The bridge domain subnet
The domain
The tenant VRF
en.explanation: Domains reference VLAN pools and are linked to AAEPs; AAEPs attach to interface policy groups so VLANs are allowed on ports.
