en.question: An EPG static port binding fails with an 'invalid VLAN' fault. What is a likely cause?
options: The VLAN is not in the pool
The bridge domain has no subnet
The contract is missing a filter
The VRF is in unenforced mode
en.explanation: The chain interface → policy group → AAEP → domain → VLAN pool must include the VLAN, and the EPG must be associated with that domain.

en.question: What does ACI VMM integration with vCenter do?
options: Maps EPGs to port groups on a VDS
Moves virtual machines between hosts automatically
Installs ESXi on the leaf switches
Backs up the vCenter database to the APIC
en.explanation: The APIC creates a VDS in vCenter; each EPG associated with the VMM domain appears as a port group, with dynamic VLAN assignment.

en.question: In ACI, a leaf receives a packet for an unknown destination IP in the same VRF. Where is it sent by default?
options: To the spine proxy (COOP database)
Flooded to every leaf in the fabric
Dropped silently at once
To the APIC for a lookup
en.explanation: Leafs send unknown unicast to the spine anycast proxy TEP; spines hold the COOP endpoint database and forward to the right leaf.

en.question: Under the NIST cloud model, which service model gives the customer virtual machines but not the OS licence management of the provider?
options: PaaS
SaaS
IaaS
FaaS only
en.explanation: IaaS provides compute, storage and network; the customer manages OS and applications. PaaS adds runtime; SaaS delivers the full app.

en.question: Which NIST deployment model is used exclusively by a single organisation, on or off premises?
options: Private cloud
Public cloud
Community cloud
Hybrid cloud
en.explanation: Private cloud is for one organisation; community is shared by organisations with common concerns; hybrid combines two or more.

en.question: Which NX-OS feature allows upgrading a Nexus switch with minimal data plane disruption?
options: Erasing the startup configuration
ISSU
Rebooting into the loader prompt
Replacing the supervisor first
en.explanation: ISSU upgrades the control plane while the data plane keeps forwarding (on supported platforms/paths); check the compatibility first.

en.question: What is EPLD on a Nexus switch?
options: A licence for extra ports on the chassis
A routing protocol for data centre links
Hardware logic upgraded separately
The vPC primary election process
en.explanation: Electronic Programmable Logic Devices hold hardware functions; EPLD images are upgraded separately and usually need a reload.

en.question: How are individual NX-OS bug fixes applied without a full upgrade?
options: Editing the running config only
Downgrading to the previous release
SMU patches
Reinstalling the BIOS on the switch
en.explanation: SMUs are installed with 'install add / activate / commit' to fix specific defects in the running release.

en.question: Which NX-OS feature lets you roll back to a previous configuration snapshot?
options: write erase and reload the switch
copy startup-config tftp
Checkpoint and rollback
reload in 10 with save
en.explanation: 'checkpoint' saves the running config; 'rollback running-config checkpoint NAME' restores it (atomic, best-effort or stop-at-first-failure).

en.question: Which feature copies traffic from source ports to a destination port for an analyser?
options: CFS
NetFlow
LLDP
SPAN
en.explanation: SPAN mirrors packets (ERSPAN sends them over GRE to a remote analyser); NetFlow exports flow records, not packets.

en.question: What is an advantage of model-driven streaming telemetry over SNMP polling?
options: It needs no external collector at all
It uses fewer YANG models per device
It only works over serial links
Devices push data at short intervals
en.explanation: Telemetry streams structured data (gRPC/gNMI, YANG paths) periodically or on change, at scale and with low latency.

en.question: What does Nexus Dashboard provide for a data centre?
options: A Fibre Channel zoning tool only
A blade server chassis manager only
A platform for fabric services
A replacement for NX-OS
en.explanation: Nexus Dashboard hosts services such as Fabric Controller, Insights and Orchestrator to manage and analyse NX-OS and ACI fabrics.

en.question: How can Cisco UCS C-Series rack servers be managed?
options: CIMC, Intersight or UCSM
Only from the APIC GUI in the fabric
Only from a serial console cable
Through vPC peer links
en.explanation: CIMC gives standalone management; servers can also be connected to Fabric Interconnects (UCSM or Intersight Managed Mode) or Intersight standalone.

en.question: Why use MAC, WWN and UUID pools in UCS service profiles?
options: Identities move with the profile
They speed up the CPU and memory
They replace VLANs in the fabric
They license the server for UCS Manager
en.explanation: Stateless computing: identities come from pools in the profile, so a profile can move to another blade without changing upstream configuration.

en.question: What is the difference between an initial and an updating service profile template in UCS Manager?
options: Initial templates update profiles on every change
Updating templates push changes to bound profiles
They are identical in every release
Updating templates cannot use pools
en.explanation: Profiles from an updating template stay bound and inherit changes (which may reboot servers); initial templates only seed profiles once.

en.question: In UCS, what is a vHBA?
options: A RAID controller setting
A virtual Ethernet NIC with a MAC
A hypervisor storage driver
A virtual FC adapter with a WWPN
en.explanation: vHBAs are defined in the service profile, get WWNN/WWPN from pools and connect to VSANs through the Fabric Interconnects.

en.question: A UCS blade must boot from a SAN LUN. What is required in the service profile?
options: A boot policy with SAN targets
A local disk policy set to any configuration
A BIOS policy disabling virtualization
An empty vNIC list
en.explanation: The boot policy lists the vHBA and the target WWPN/LUN; zoning and LUN masking on the storage must allow the initiator.

en.question: What is Intersight Managed Mode (IMM) for UCS X-Series?
options: Managing servers only from local CIMC
Intersight managing FIs and servers
An ACI mode for leaf switches
A storage array firmware mode
en.explanation: In IMM, Intersight manages FIs, chassis and servers using pools, policies and server profiles; UCS X-Series requires it (no UCSM).

en.question: What does a host firmware package in UCS ensure?
options: Automatic VLAN creation on uplinks
Faster DIMM speeds
Consistent firmware versions
Licence activation for each blade
en.explanation: Firmware packages (or Intersight firmware policies) define BIOS, adapter and controller versions applied when the profile is associated.

en.question: Which UCS Manager backup type can restore the whole system on a replaced Fabric Interconnect pair?
options: Tech-support file
Logical configuration export only
System event log export
Full state backup
en.explanation: Full state is a binary snapshot for disaster recovery; all-configuration, logical and system exports are XML for importing settings.

en.question: How can you capture traffic from a UCS server vNIC for analysis?
options: Export a full state backup
Enable debug logging in the BIOS
Use the KVM console of the server
A traffic monitoring session on the FI
en.explanation: UCS Manager traffic monitoring sessions mirror vNIC/vHBA or uplink traffic to a destination port on the FI.

en.question: What is a VSAN on Cisco MDS and Nexus switches?
options: A vPC domain for storage ports
A VLAN that carries iSCSI traffic only
A storage array volume on a disk
A virtual SAN fabric
en.explanation: VSANs isolate Fibre Channel fabrics on shared hardware; each runs its own fabric services (FSPF, zoning, name server).

en.question: During Fibre Channel fabric initialisation, what does the principal switch do?
options: Holds every zone member's data
Assigns domain IDs to switches
Encrypts all FC frames
Elects the vPC primary
en.explanation: Principal switch selection happens per VSAN; it allocates domain IDs, which form the first byte of each FCID.

en.question: What are the three parts of an FCID?
options: VSAN, VLAN and port
Domain, area and port
WWNN, WWPN and LUN
Site, rack and slot number
en.explanation: The 24-bit FCID is domain (switch), area and port; it is assigned at fabric login (FLOGI).

en.question: What is the purpose of zoning in a Fibre Channel SAN?
options: Assign FCIDs to the hosts
Limit which initiators see which targets
Bundle ISLs into a port channel
Set the MTU of the VSAN uplinks
en.explanation: Zones (usually single-initiator, single-target, or smart zoning) limit communication; zonesets are activated per VSAN.

en.question: What does enhanced zoning add over basic zoning?
options: A fabric-wide change lock
Zones that span several VSANs
Encryption of zone members
Automatic LUN masking on arrays
en.explanation: Enhanced zoning uses a session lock so only one admin edits at a time, then commits atomically; basic zoning can overwrite changes.

en.question: Which command shows the devices logged in to the Fibre Channel name server?
options: show zone active
show flogi interface status
show fcns database
show vsan membership
en.explanation: The FCNS database lists FCIDs, WWPNs and FC4 types for the VSAN; 'show flogi database' lists local logins.

en.question: Why use device aliases in an MDS fabric?
options: Replacing zones with VSANs
Faster FC frame forwarding
Extra buffer credits on each ISL
Names for WWPNs, shared by CFS
en.explanation: Device aliases map names to pWWNs and are distributed fabric-wide via CFS, so zones are readable and easy to update when HBAs change.

en.question: What does NPV mode on a UCS Fabric Interconnect or Nexus switch do?
options: Blocks all FLOGIs from the hosts
Turns the switch into a full FC switch
Proxies host logins to the core
Runs FSPF to the core switches
en.explanation: In NPV the edge switch proxies FLOGIs as FDISCs to an NPIV-enabled core, avoiding domain ID use and interop issues.

en.question: What must be enabled on the core switch for NPV edge switches to connect?
options: feature lacp
feature npv
feature fport-channel-trunk only
feature npiv
en.explanation: NPIV lets one F port accept multiple N port logins (FDISC); the core needs NPIV while the edge runs NPV.

en.question: Why bundle ISLs between two MDS switches into a SAN port channel?
options: More bandwidth and resilience
To merge two VSANs into one
To disable zoning between the switches
To assign new domain IDs to both
en.explanation: A SAN port channel appears as one logical ISL: traffic is balanced and a member failure does not trigger FSPF reconvergence.

en.question: What does CFS do on MDS and Nexus switches?
options: Compresses FC frames on long links
Shares feature config across switches
Creates VSANs automatically on boot
Monitors fan speed in the chassis
en.explanation: Cisco Fabric Services distributes and locks configuration (device alias, NTP, port security, etc.) across the fabric.

en.question: Which protocol carries SCSI commands over a standard TCP/IP network?
options: iSCSI
FCoE
NFS
FSPF
en.explanation: iSCSI uses TCP 3260; FCoE carries FC frames directly over lossless Ethernet; NFS is file-level storage.

en.question: What is the key difference between NFS and iSCSI storage?
options: NFS needs Fibre Channel switches
NFS is file; iSCSI is block
iSCSI only runs on InfiniBand
They are the same protocol
en.explanation: NFS is a network file system (NAS); iSCSI gives the host a block device that it formats itself.

en.question: What should be checked before a nondisruptive MDS software upgrade?
options: That every zone is deactivated
The 'show install all impact' output
That all ISLs are shut down
That the FCNS database is cleared
en.explanation: 'show install all impact' reports whether modules upgrade hitlessly; dual supervisors and compatible versions allow nondisruptive upgrades.

en.question: Which MDS feature analyses SCSI/NVMe I/O performance per flow?
options: SAN Analytics
Port security
Device alias
Zone merge
en.explanation: SAN Analytics (with SAN Insights in Nexus Dashboard) inspects frames on supported modules to report latency, IOPS and errors per initiator-target-LUN.

en.question: What does the Embedded Event Manager (EEM) do on NX-OS?
options: Balances traffic over ISLs
Upgrades software every week
Runs actions on defined events
Syncs the vPC config to the peer
en.explanation: EEM applets match events (syslog, counters, CLI) and run actions such as CLI commands or scripts.

en.question: Which NX-OS feature runs jobs (such as config backups) at set times?
options: EEM tracking
Scheduler
Checkpoint
POAP
en.explanation: feature scheduler defines jobs and schedules (e.g. daily copy running-config to a server).

en.question: What is the difference between Bash shell and Guest Shell on NX-OS?
options: They are the same environment with other names
Guest Shell is an isolated container
Guest Shell needs an external server
Bash only runs Python 2 scripts
en.explanation: Bash gives native Linux access to the switch; Guest Shell is a CentOS-based LXC container for running apps and Python safely.

en.question: What does NX-API CLI let a script do?
options: Read SNMP traps from the switch
Replace NX-OS with Linux
Configure only the BIOS settings
Send CLI over HTTPS, get JSON
en.explanation: NX-API (feature nxapi) accepts JSON-RPC/ins_api requests with show or config commands and returns structured output.

en.question: On-box Python on NX-OS uses which module to run CLI commands?
options: requests
netmiko
paramiko
cli
en.explanation: The on-box cli module provides cli(), clid() (JSON) and clip(); off-box tools like netmiko use SSH.

en.question: Why is Ansible popular for data centre network automation?
options: It needs an agent on each switch
It is agentless, using YAML playbooks
It only works with UCS servers
It compiles playbooks to firmware
en.explanation: Ansible connects to devices with network_cli or httpapi (e.g. cisco.nxos, cisco.aci collections), using idempotent modules.

en.question: What does POAP do on a new Nexus switch?
options: Creates a vPC peer link to its neighbour
Joins an ACI fabric automatically
Uses DHCP to fetch image and config
Runs Terraform from the bootflash
en.explanation: Power-On Auto Provisioning uses DHCP options to find a script server, then the script fetches image and configuration.

en.question: What does Terraform's 'plan' step do with the ACI provider?
options: Backs up the APIC config first
Applies all changes at once
Deletes and recreates the tenant
Shows the planned changes
en.explanation: terraform plan compares desired state with state/real objects; apply then creates, updates or destroys resources.

en.question: Which interfaces can automate Cisco Intersight?
options: Only SNMP get requests
Only the web GUI
REST API, SDKs and Terraform
Only the serial console of each server
en.explanation: Intersight exposes an OpenAPI REST interface with API keys, SDKs, a Terraform provider and Ansible modules.

en.question: Why do AI/ML training clusters need lossless Ethernet features like PFC and ECN?
options: RoCEv2 traffic suffers from drops
GPUs use only Fibre Channel
They need spanning tree on all links
To reduce the MAC table size on leafs
en.explanation: RDMA over Converged Ethernet expects no loss; PFC pauses per priority and ECN/DCQCN signals congestion before drops.

en.question: Which protocol is preferred for device administration AAA because it can authorise each command?
options: TACACS+
RADIUS
LDAP
SNMPv2c
en.explanation: TACACS+ separates authentication, authorisation and accounting and supports per-command authorisation.

en.question: In ACI, what must exist for two EPGs to communicate?
options: A contract between them
A shared VLAN ID on both
The same IP subnet
A static route on the leaf
en.explanation: ACI is whitelist by default: one EPG provides and another consumes a contract whose subjects and filters allow traffic.

en.question: What does microsegmentation (uSeg EPG) in ACI allow?
options: Encrypting the whole fabric
Splitting a leaf into two switches
Grouping endpoints by attributes
Creating VSANs for the VMs
en.explanation: uSeg EPGs classify endpoints by attributes (IP, MAC, VM name, OS…) so policy applies even within the same BD/port group.

en.question: Which first-hop security feature blocks rogue DHCP servers on access ports?
options: Storm control
DHCP snooping
BPDU guard
UDLD
en.explanation: DHCP snooping trusts only uplink ports for server messages and builds a binding table used by DAI and IP Source Guard.

en.question: Why configure a keychain on NX-OS routing protocols?
options: To speed up convergence
To encrypt user data
To store local passwords
To rotate auth keys
en.explanation: Keychains hold multiple keys with send/accept lifetimes, allowing hitless rollover for OSPF, EIGRP, BGP or HSRP authentication.

en.question: What does MACsec provide on a link between two Nexus switches?
options: End-to-end IPsec tunnels
Layer 2 link encryption
DHCP protection on the link
Faster LACP negotiation
en.explanation: MACsec (802.1AE) encrypts frames on each link at line rate, with keys from MKA (pre-shared key or 802.1X).

en.question: What does port security on an MDS switch do?
options: Creates zones automatically
Encrypts the FC frames
Limits ISL bandwidth
Binds WWNs to ports
en.explanation: Port security restricts which devices (pWWN/nWWN/sWWN) may log in on which interfaces; violating logins are rejected.

en.question: How does fabric binding differ from port security on MDS?
options: It encrypts traffic on ISLs
It controls hosts on F ports
It controls which switches join
It replaces zoning in the VSAN
en.explanation: Fabric binding authorises switch WWNs (and domain IDs) on E/TE ports, preventing unauthorised switches from merging into the fabric.

pt.question: Que oferta da Cisco dá chamadas baseadas no Unified CM alojadas pela Cisco numa cloud privada dedicada?
options: Cisco Unity Express em routers de filial
Só o Webex Calling multi-tenant
Webex Calling Dedicated Instance
Um único CUBE local com SRST
pt.explanation: O Dedicated Instance corre o UCM, Unity Connection e Expressway próprios do cliente nos centros de dados Webex, gerido pela Cisco/parceiro e integrado com o Webex.

pt.question: Que ferramenta se usa para dimensionar uma implementação Cisco Collaboration (servidores e VM)?
options: O Expressway Configuration Wizard
A Collaboration Sizing Tool
A ferramenta Call Flow do RTMT
A página Analytics do Webex Control Hub
pt.explanation: A Cisco Collaboration Sizing Tool (com as orientações de virtualização) estima nós e tamanhos de OVA a partir de utilizadores, equipamentos e tráfego.

pt.question: Uma chamada G.711 sobre Ethernet usa cerca de quanta largura de banda por sentido, incluindo o overhead L2 (pacotes de 20 ms)?
options: Cerca de 87 kb/s
Cerca de 8 kb/s
Exatamente 64 kb/s
Cerca de 300 kb/s
pt.explanation: 64 kb/s de carga mais cabeçalhos RTP/UDP/IP (40 B) e Ethernet (18 B) a 50 pps dão cerca de 87 kb/s; o G.729 é cerca de 31 kb/s.

pt.question: Que codec de áudio é de banda larga, adapta o débito e é muito usado pelo Webex e pelos endpoints modernos?
options: G.711 µ-law
Opus
pt.explanation: O Opus suporta de banda estreita a banda total, débito variável e resiliência a perdas; o G.711 é de banda estreita a 64 kb/s.

pt.question: Como dá o Unified CM redundância de processamento de chamadas aos telefones?
options: Um único publisher que trata de todos os registos
Um CM group com subscribers primário e de reserva
Só um par HSRP de servidores TFTP
Um segundo cluster com os mesmos endereços IP
pt.explanation: O Unified CM group do device pool define a ordem dos subscribers; os telefones registam-se no primeiro e passam para o seguinte em caso de falha.

pt.question: Que funcionalidade do UCM faz cópia da configuração do cluster para recuperação de desastres?
options: Disaster Recovery System (DRS)
Exportação do Bulk Administration Tool
Recolha de traces do RTMT
CDR Analysis and Reporting
pt.explanation: O DRS faz cópia da base de dados do publisher e dos componentes para um servidor SFTP e repõe-nos após uma reconstrução.

pt.question: Porque se usa SRTP nos endpoints de colaboração?
options: Cifra os media de voz e vídeo
Cifra só a sinalização SIP
Comprime cabeçalhos RTP em ligações WAN
Autentica utilizadores no LDAP
pt.explanation: O SRTP protege a confidencialidade e integridade dos media; o TLS protege a sinalização SIP, que também leva as chaves SRTP (SDES).

pt.question: Qual é o papel principal do Expressway-C e Expressway-E em conjunto?
options: Travessia de firewall para remoto e B2B
Alojar caixas de voicemail para utilizadores remotos
Substituir o UCM como agente de controlo de chamadas
Funcionar como servidor TFTP do cluster
pt.explanation: O Expressway-E na DMZ e o Expressway-C no interior criam uma traversal zone, permitindo Mobile and Remote Access (MRA) e chamadas B2B sem VPN.

pt.question: Para que se usa normalmente o CUBE?
options: Um controlador sem fios para telefones IP
Um elemento de fronteira SIP para trunks
Um servidor de presença para chat e estado
Um diretório LDAP de utilizadores
pt.explanation: O Cisco Unified Border Element em routers IOS XE demarca trunks SIP: interoperabilidade, segurança, normalização e tratamento de media.

pt.question: Numa atualização de um cluster UCM, que nó é atualizado primeiro?
options: Sempre o nó só de TFTP
Qualquer subscriber do grupo
O publisher
Todos os nós em paralelo de uma vez
pt.explanation: O publisher é atualizado primeiro, depois os subscribers (em grupos), e depois faz-se o switch version no publisher antes dos subscribers.

pt.question: O SSO SAML do UCM falha com um erro de asserção relacionado com o tempo. O que se deve verificar primeiro?
options: A CSS da linha do utilizador
O phone button template
O NTP no UCM e no IdP
A ordem da route list
pt.explanation: As asserções SAML têm janelas de validade; a diferença de relógio entre o UCM e o fornecedor de identidade faz que sejam rejeitadas.

pt.question: Porque deve o certificado do Expressway-E ser assinado por uma CA pública?
options: Permite aos telefones saltar o TFTP
Os clientes de fora têm de confiar nele
As CA públicas dão chaves mais compridas
O Expressway-C exige-o para o LDAP
pt.explanation: Os clientes MRA e os parceiros B2B validam o certificado do Expressway-E; os SAN têm de incluir o domínio MRA e outros nomes necessários.

pt.question: O que melhora o OAuth com refresh tokens para os utilizadores da Webex App no UCM?
options: Maior resolução de vídeo nas chamadas
Menos pedidos de password
Descarga mais rápida dos ficheiros TFTP
Criação automática do plano de marcação
pt.explanation: Os clientes recebem tokens de acesso e de refresh após autenticar, por isso voltam a ligar-se (também por MRA) sem reintroduzir credenciais.

pt.question: Um trunk SIP TLS para o CUBE falha durante o handshake. Qual é uma causa comum?
options: O DTMF está definido como KPML
O trunk usa G.711 em vez de G.729
O route pattern não tem partição
A CA do par não é de confiança
pt.explanation: Cada lado tem de confiar na cadeia de certificados do outro (e os nomes têm de coincidir se forem verificados); caso contrário o handshake TLS falha.

pt.question: As chamadas entre dois telefones seguros não mostram cadeado e usam RTP. Qual é uma razão provável?
options: Os telefones têm o Opus desligado
Os telefones usam o toque errado
As chamadas passam por um hunt pilot
A sinalização não usa TLS
pt.explanation: As chaves SRTP trocam-se na sinalização; se esta não estiver cifrada (TLS) o sistema volta ao RTP.

pt.question: Que registo DNS permite à Webex App e aos clientes MRA descobrirem o Expressway a partir da internet?
options: Registo PTR de cada telefone
Registo A do servidor TFTP
SRV _collab-edge._tls
Registo MX do domínio
pt.explanation: Os clientes externos procuram _collab-edge._tls.<domínio>; internamente procuram _cisco-uds._tcp para encontrar o UCM.

pt.question: Que opção DHCP dá aos telefones IP Cisco o endereço do servidor TFTP?
options: Opção 43
Opção 150
Opção 82
Opção 66 só para Cisco
pt.explanation: A opção 150 indica um ou mais servidores TFTP para os telefones Cisco (a opção 66 é o nome TFTP único padrão).

pt.question: Como aprende um telefone IP a sua VLAN de voz a partir de um switch Cisco?
options: Mensagens SIP REGISTER
Opção 150 de DHCP
O ficheiro de config TFTP
CDP ou LLDP-MED
pt.explanation: O switch anuncia a VLAN de voz por CDP (ou LLDP-MED); o telefone etiqueta o seu tráfego e pede DHCP nessa VLAN.

pt.question: Os utilizadores não conseguem entrar no Self Care com as passwords do AD, mas a sincronização funciona. O que falta?
options: O perfil de voicemail do utilizador
Agenda de sincronização do diretório LDAP
Uma partição na linha
Autenticação LDAP no UCM
pt.explanation: A sincronização LDAP importa os utilizadores; a autenticação LDAP também tem de estar ativa para o UCM validar as passwords no AD.

pt.question: O que permite o self-provisioning no UCM?
options: Os utilizadores criam route patterns no Self Care
Os telefones escolhem o seu próprio número
Os utilizadores associam o telefone por IVR
Os telefones descarregam firmware da internet
pt.explanation: Com auto-registo e um IVR de self-provisioning, os utilizadores autenticam-se com PIN e o telefone é criado pelo seu perfil/templates.

pt.question: Que ferramenta do UCM acrescenta centenas de telefones e utilizadores a partir de ficheiros CSV?
options: Bulk Administration Tool
Dialed Number Analyzer
Real-Time Monitoring Tool
Disaster Recovery System
pt.explanation: O BAT usa templates e ficheiros CSV para inserir, alterar ou apagar telefones, utilizadores e linhas em massa.

pt.question: Como se pode integrar um telefone com um código de ativação?
options: O código é enviado na opção 150 de DHCP
O administrador escreve o MAC no Expressway
O telefone procura o UCM na rede
O utilizador escreve o código no telefone
pt.explanation: Os códigos de ativação evitam introduzir MAC: o telefone contacta o serviço de ativação (ou o UCM) com o código e recebe a configuração, também por MRA.

pt.question: Que resposta SIP indica que o telefone chamado está a tocar?
options: 100 Trying
200 OK
180 Ringing
486 Busy Here
pt.explanation: O 100 Trying é progresso salto a salto, o 180/183 indica toque/early media, o 200 OK atende; o 486 significa ocupado.

pt.question: Uma chamada SIP é atendida mas cai ao fim de cerca de 30 segundos. Qual é uma causa típica?
options: O DTMF usa RFC 2833
O INVITE não tem corpo SDP
O telefone não está registado
O ACK nunca chega
pt.explanation: Sem ACK, o lado que atendeu retransmite o 200 OK e termina após o temporizador (~32 s), muitas vezes por NAT/firewall ou problemas de encaminhamento.

pt.question: O que descreve a linha 'm=' do SDP?
options: O nome apresentado do chamador
Tipo de media, porta e codecs
O endereço do servidor SIP
A duração da chamada
pt.explanation: m=audio 16384 RTP/AVP 0 101 dá o tipo de media, a porta RTP, o perfil de transporte e os payload types; o c= dá o IP.

pt.question: Como são enviados os dígitos DTMF com o RFC 2833/4733?
options: Como mensagens SIP INFO
Como telephone events RTP
Só como tons de áudio na banda
Como subscrições KPML
pt.explanation: O RFC 2833/4733 leva o DTMF como payload RTP (normalmente o tipo 101), negociado no SDP; o SIP INFO e o KPML são métodos de sinalização.

pt.question: Como coloca normalmente um telefone SIP uma chamada em espera?
options: Uma resposta 486 ao par
Um BYE seguido de um novo INVITE
Um REGISTER com expires=0
Um re-INVITE com sendonly
pt.explanation: A espera é um re-INVITE que muda a direção dos media; depois pode entrar a música de espera; retomar envia um re-INVITE com sendrecv.

pt.question: Que método SIP se usa numa transferência?
options: SUBSCRIBE
REFER
OPTIONS
PRACK
pt.explanation: O REFER pede ao transferido que ligue para o destino (com Replaces na transferência assistida); o NOTIFY informa o progresso.

pt.question: Um telefone SIP mostra 'A registar' e nunca se regista no UCM. Qual é uma causa comum?
options: O equipamento não está configurado
A route list tem membros a mais
A CSS do telefone não tem a partição PSTN
A música de espera está desligada
pt.explanation: O registo precisa do equipamento no UCM (ou auto-registo), TFTP/config corretos e, se usado, credenciais digest certas; veja o RTMT e os logs do telefone.

pt.question: No UCM, que elemento decide a que partições um equipamento chamador pode chegar?
options: Calling search space
Media resource group
Device pool
Region entre sites
pt.explanation: Uma CSS é uma lista ordenada de partições; a CSS da linha e a do equipamento combinam-se (a da linha primeiro) no encaminhamento.

pt.question: Dois route patterns coincidem com um número marcado: 9.1XXX e 9.1[2-9]XX. Qual é escolhido para 91234?
options: Ambos, em round-robin
9.1XXX
Nenhum; a chamada falha
pt.explanation: O UCM escolhe a coincidência mais próxima (mais específica): [2-9] corresponde a 8 valores contra 10 do X, por isso ganha 9.1[2-9]XX.

pt.question: Que definição do UCM ajuda a evitar fraude telefónica por reencaminhamento para números internacionais?
options: Uma CSS de forward restrita
Mais largura de banda na região
Ativar o auto-registo
Usar só G.711 nos trunks
pt.explanation: Restringir a CSS do Call Forward All (e bloquear padrões internacionais, usar FAC e horários) impede reencaminhar para números caros.

pt.question: Qual é a diferença entre um route group e uma route list?
options: Um route group aponta para route patterns
São o mesmo objeto no UCM
A list ordena grupos de equipamentos
Uma route list contém telefones
pt.explanation: Route pattern → route list (route groups por ordem, com local route group) → route group (gateways/trunks por ordem com algoritmo de distribuição).

pt.question: Num plano de marcação globalizado, onde é normalizado o número chamado para +E.164?
options: No softkey template do telefone
Só no dial peer POTS do gateway
Em translation patterns
Na região do device pool
pt.explanation: O encaminhamento globalizado normaliza os números à entrada (translation patterns, transformações chamada/chamador) e localiza-os à saída.

pt.question: O que permite o local route group (LRG)?
options: Atribuir telefones a partições
Encaminhar todas as chamadas para um só local
Desligar as route lists de cada site
Um padrão, gateway local por site
pt.explanation: O LRG associa-se por device pool, por isso um único route pattern +E.164 envia as chamadas pelo gateway local do chamador sem padrões por local.

pt.question: Como se configura o encaminhamento por hora do dia no UCM?
options: Uma tarefa cron no publisher
Time schedules nas partições
Uma definição no firmware do telefone
Um algoritmo de distribuição do route group
pt.explanation: Os time schedules feitos de time periods atribuem-se a partições; fora do horário, os padrões dessa partição não são alcançáveis.

pt.question: O que é um forced authorization code (FAC)?
options: Um código para certas chamadas
Um PIN da caixa de voicemail
Uma chave de licença do trunk
Uma regra de negociação de codecs
pt.explanation: O FAC num route pattern exige um código de nível de autorização antes de certas chamadas (p. ex. internacionais) avançarem e regista-o nos CDR.

pt.question: Porque se ativa 'Urgent Priority' num route pattern de emergência como o 112?
options: Ignora todas as partições
Dá mais QoS às chamadas de emergência
Encaminha sem esperar
Grava a chamada para revisão
pt.explanation: A urgent priority termina a recolha de dígitos em sobreposição, por isso o 112 encaminha de imediato mesmo que existam padrões como 112X.

pt.question: Que ferramenta do UCM mostra como seria encaminhado um número marcado a partir de um equipamento?
options: Cisco Unified Reporting
Bulk Administration Tool
Disaster Recovery System
Dialed Number Analyzer
pt.explanation: O DNA simula a análise de dígitos com a CSS do equipamento chamador e mostra os padrões coincidentes, transformações e o caminho escolhido.

pt.question: Que API do UCM é baseada em SOAP e se usa para provisionar utilizadores, telefones e linhas?
options: JTAPI
UDS
CTI
AXL
pt.explanation: O AXL (Administrative XML) é uma API SOAP/XML com autenticação básica para provisionamento; o UDS é uma API REST sobretudo para dados de utilizadores/equipamentos.

pt.question: O que faz o MWI para uma caixa de correio do Unity Connection?
options: Acende a luz de mensagens
Grava a saudação do utilizador
Transcreve o voicemail para texto
Define o tamanho máximo da caixa
pt.explanation: O Unity Connection sinaliza o UCM (pela integração SIP/SCCP, com DN de MWI on/off) para acender o indicador quando há mensagens novas.

pt.question: Como se integra hoje mais frequentemente o Unity Connection com o UCM?
options: Um gateway analógico
Só portas de voicemail SCCP
Gatekeeper H.323
Um trunk SIP
pt.explanation: Uma integração por trunk SIP aponta o voicemail pilot do UCM para o Unity Connection; as portas SCCP são a opção antiga.

pt.question: No Unity Connection, o que decide que call handler atende uma chamada recebida?
options: As routing rules
A CSS do telefone
A route list no UCM
O device pool da porta
pt.explanation: As routing rules verificam condições (número chamador/marcado, porta, horário) e enviam chamadas diretas ou reencaminhadas para um call handler, interview handler ou conversa.

pt.question: Como se dá acesso por funções a uma equipa de helpdesk na administração do UCM?
options: Um segundo nó publisher
Partições separadas para cada admin
Um device pool diferente
Access control groups
pt.explanation: Os utilizadores (locais ou LDAP) entram em access control groups cujas funções definem direitos de leitura/alteração nas páginas do UCM.

pt.question: Que comando de dial peer ativa o DTMF relay RFC 2833 num dial peer SIP do CUBE?
options: dtmf-relay cisco-rtp sip
dtmf-relay h245-alphanumeric
dtmf-relay rtp-nte
codec dtmf inband
pt.explanation: O rtp-nte envia named telephone events no RTP; sip-kpml e sip-notify são opções de sinalização; o h245 é para H.323.

pt.question: Uma voice translation rule é rule 1 /^0\(.*\)/ /+351\1/. O que faz a 0211234567?
options: Deixa-o igual
Apaga todos os dígitos
pt.explanation: A regex identifica o 0 inicial, captura o resto e substitui por +351 seguido dos dígitos capturados.

pt.question: Como se aplica uma voice translation rule às chamadas de um dial peer?
options: Num translation profile
Diretamente com 'rule' no peer
Só através de um SIP profile
Através da codec class
pt.explanation: As regras ficam numa voice translation-rule; um voice translation-profile refere-as para números chamado/chamador e associa-se ao dial peer.

pt.question: O que define uma voice class codec no CUBE?
options: Codecs a oferecer, por ordem
O número de DSP de cada codec
A largura de banda da ligação WAN
O método DTMF do trunk
pt.explanation: A voice class codec N lista as preferências de codecs; o dial peer refere-a para o CUBE oferecer/aceitar codecs por essa ordem.

pt.question: Qual é a diferença entre dial peers POTS e VoIP?
options: Os POTS são só para chamadas de fax
POTS: portas de voz; VoIP: destinos IP
Os VoIP são só para telefones analógicos
Não há diferença prática
pt.explanation: Os dial peers POTS usam 'port' (FXS/FXO/E1/T1); os VoIP usam session target (IP/DNS/server group) e session protocol.

pt.question: Como deteta o CUBE que um par de trunk SIP está em baixo e deixa de lhe enviar chamadas?
options: Keepalive SIP OPTIONS no dial peer
Monitorizando sessões BFD para o ITSP
Esperando que o ITSP envie um BYE
Verificando o estado da DSP farm
pt.explanation: A voice class sip-options-keepalive põe o dial peer em busy-out quando os OPTIONS não têm resposta, e passa a usar outro peer/membro do server group.

pt.question: O que dá uma voice class server-group no CUBE?
options: Balanceamento de DSP
Um cluster de routers CUBE
Vários destinos por peer
Uma lista de servidores LDAP
pt.explanation: Um server group lista IP de destino com preferência ou round-robin, referido por session server-group no dial peer.

pt.question: Uma chamada recebida no CUBE coincide com o dial peer de entrada errado. Que comando ajuda a coincidir por um URI ou IP?
options: dtmf-relay rtp-nte
destination-pattern no peer POTS
codec preference 1 g711ulaw
incoming uri via
pt.explanation: A coincidência de entrada pode usar incoming uri (from/to/via/request) com uma voice class uri, ou números chamado/chamador; o 'show dial-peer voice summary' e o debug ccsip ajudam.

pt.question: O que permite mudar um SIP profile no CUBE?
options: A tabela de encaminhamento do router
O firmware DSP dos codecs
Normalização de cabeçalhos SIP
O temporizador de registo dos telefones
pt.explanation: As voice class sip-profiles acrescentam, mudam ou removem cabeçalhos SIP/SDP para interoperar com operadores; aplicam-se por dial peer ou globalmente.

pt.question: Porque usar voice class tenants num CUBE com vários trunks?
options: Para isolar DSP por cliente
Definições SIP por operador
Para faturar cada departamento
Para licenciar cada dial peer
pt.explanation: Os tenants agrupam definições SIP globais (bind, registrar, credenciais, temporizadores) por operador, para cada trunk ter a sua configuração.

pt.question: Que recurso de media IOS XE é preciso para conferências ou transcodificação com codecs diferentes?
options: Uma porta do Unity Connection
Um trunk SIP extra
Recursos de DSP farm
Um route group
pt.explanation: Os perfis DSP farm (conferência, transcodificação, MTP) registam-se no UCM como recursos de media e usam os DSP do router.

pt.question: Que aplicações compõem o Webex Suite para os utilizadores finais?
options: Só provisionamento de telefones IP
Só salas de videoconferência
Chamadas, reuniões, mensagens
Só agentes de contact centre
pt.explanation: O Webex Suite junta chamadas, reuniões, mensagens, webinars, sondagens e mais na Webex App e nos equipamentos.

pt.question: No Webex Calling, como é encaminhada uma chamada de um utilizador para um número externo quando o local usa um Local Gateway?
options: Pelo trunk LGW do local
Diretamente do telefone para o ITSP
Pelo operador móvel do utilizador
Através do Unity Connection
pt.explanation: O Webex Calling encaminha as chamadas PSTN pela ligação de cada local (Cisco PSTN, CCP, ou nas instalações por um trunk Local Gateway).

pt.question: Que funcionalidade do Webex Calling impede os utilizadores de fazer chamadas internacionais?
options: Políticas de gravação
Mascaramento de números
Permissões de chamada
Definições de Caller ID
pt.explanation: As permissões de chamadas por local ou utilizador permitem/bloqueiam tipos de chamada (internacionais, premium) e podem exigir códigos de autorização.

pt.question: No Webex Calling, o que é um local (location)?
options: Um site com números e PSTN
Um equipamento de sala de reuniões
A morada de casa de um utilizador
Uma função de admin do Control Hub
pt.explanation: Os locais definem a morada de emergência, fuso horário, números, ligação PSTN e definições de marcação interna para utilizadores e equipamentos.

pt.question: No Webex Calling, como se relacionam trunks e route groups?
options: Os route groups substituem os dial plans
Os trunks contêm route groups
São o mesmo tipo de objeto
Route groups agrupam trunks
pt.explanation: Os trunks ligam a Local Gateways; os route groups combinam trunks com prioridades; os dial plans ou locais apontam depois para um trunk ou route group.

pt.question: Para que se usa um dial plan do Webex Calling?
options: Enviar padrões para trunks PBX
Atribuir números a utilizadores
Gravar as chamadas externas
Mudar os toques de cada local
pt.explanation: Os dial plans contêm padrões (números da empresa) encaminhados para um trunk/route group, deixando os utilizadores Webex chegar a números do UCM ou PBX locais.

pt.question: Onde se gerem as definições do site Webex Meetings, como o áudio por omissão e a gravação?
options: Na admin do Unity Connection
Na página web de cada telefone
No route plan do UCM
No Control Hub
pt.explanation: Os sites de reuniões configuram-se no Control Hub (antigo Site Admin): áudio, gravação, segurança e privilégios dos utilizadores.

pt.question: Que definição do Control Hub pode impedir os utilizadores de partilhar ficheiros nas mensagens Webex com organizações externas?
options: Permissões de chamadas
Definições de mensagens
Bloqueio do site de reuniões
Directory Connector
pt.explanation: As definições de mensagens do Control Hub incluem comunicação externa, restrições de partilha de ficheiros, retenção e funcionalidades Pro Pack/Extended Security.

pt.question: Que tipo de API expõe o Webex aos programadores?
options: REST com JSON
Só SOAP/XML
MIB SNMP
CLI por Telnet
pt.explanation: As API Webex em webexapis.com são REST com corpos JSON, mais SDK e webhooks.

pt.question: Como atua uma integração em nome de um utilizador Webex?
options: A password do utilizador em cada chamada
Um token de acesso OAuth 2.0
Um token de bot partilhado por todos
Uma chave de API no URL
pt.explanation: As integrações usam o fluxo authorization code do OAuth com scopes; os bots têm token próprio; as service apps usam tokens autorizados pelo admin.

pt.question: Como notifica um webhook Webex a sua aplicação?
options: Um ciclo de consulta no seu código
Um HTTP POST a cada evento
Um trunk SIP para o Webex
Um relatório do Control Hub
pt.explanation: Regista-se um webhook (resource + event + targetUrl); o Webex chama o seu endpoint quando, por exemplo, é criada uma mensagem.

pt.question: Como podem os utilizadores ser provisionados automaticamente no Control Hub a partir de um fornecedor de identidade como o Entra ID?
options: CDR
Traps SNMP
SCIM
Ficheiros TFTP
pt.explanation: O SCIM 2.0 a partir do Entra ID/Okta cria e atualiza utilizadores; o Directory Connector sincroniza a partir do AD local. As funções RBAC controlam os direitos de admin.

pt.question: O que dá o Webex Cloud-Connected UC (CCUC) ao UCM local?
options: Uma ligação PSTN gratuita por site
Mudar todos os utilizadores para Webex Calling
Visão cloud dos clusters UCM
Substituir o Unity Connection
pt.explanation: O CCUC liga clusters UCM ao Control Hub para analítica, gestão de certificados, informação de atualizações e outros serviços cloud.

pt.question: Que Webex Hybrid Service permite aos utilizadores agendar reuniões Webex a partir do calendário Exchange/Microsoft 365?
options: Hybrid Data Security
Hybrid Calendar
Video Mesh
Só Hybrid Directory
pt.explanation: O Hybrid Calendar integra calendários Exchange, Microsoft 365 ou Google para pôr botões de entrada (OBTP) e agendar com @webex.

pt.question: O que faz o Webex Video Mesh?
options: Grava as chamadas no local
Cifra mensagens com chaves locais
Sincroniza utilizadores do AD com a cloud
Mantém media de reuniões no local
pt.explanation: Os nós Video Mesh alojam localmente os media das reuniões para poupar largura de banda internet e melhorar a qualidade, em cascata com a cloud quando preciso.

pt.question: Uma chamada tem áudio só num sentido. Qual é a causa mais comum?
options: O codec é G.711 em vez de G.722
RTP bloqueado num sentido
O telefone tem o toque errado
A CSS do utilizador está errada
pt.explanation: A sinalização funciona mas o RTP não chega a um lado: falta de rotas, ACL, problemas de NAT/ALG ou endereço de media errado no SDP.

pt.question: Os utilizadores falam de áudio entrecortado nas horas de ponta na WAN. Qual é a causa provável?
options: Os telefones usam o nome de VLAN errado
Faltam registos DNS SRV
Perdas e jitter por congestionamento
A sincronização LDAP está atrasada
pt.explanation: O congestionamento sem QoS causa perdas e atraso variável; verifique descartes nas interfaces, filas e estatísticas RTP (jitter/perdas) nos telefones.

pt.question: Que marcações DSCP se recomendam para os media de voz e a sinalização de chamadas?
options: Default (0) para os dois tipos
AF41 para voz, EF para sinalização
CS1 para voz, CS7 para sinalização
EF voz, CS3 sinalização
pt.explanation: A base de QoS da Cisco usa EF para os media de voz, CS3 para a sinalização e AF41 para vídeo interativo.

pt.question: Porque é mais difícil o QoS de voz em Wi-Fi do que em ligações com fios?
options: Airtime partilhado e filas WMM
O Wi-Fi não leva DSCP de todo
A rede sem fios só suporta G.729
Os AP não podem usar VLAN
pt.explanation: O WMM mapeia DSCP/UP em categorias de acesso; a contenção, as retransmissões e o roaming acrescentam jitter, por isso desenhe cobertura, CAC e roaming rápido.

pt.question: Onde se define normalmente a fronteira de confiança para um telefone IP Cisco com um PC atrás?
options: Na placa de rede do PC
No telefone IP
Só no router da WAN
No operador de internet
pt.explanation: O switch de acesso estende a confiança ao telefone (por CDP); o telefone remarca o tráfego do PC, por isso as marcações do próprio PC não são de confiança.

pt.question: Que configuração cria uma fila de baixa latência para voz numa interface WAN IOS XE?
options: police 64000; match any; service-policy input na LAN
class-map match dscp ef; policy-map bandwidth remaining; service-policy input
access-list 101 permit udp; ip route; interface priority
class-map match dscp ef; policy-map class priority; service-policy output
pt.explanation: O LLQ usa o comando 'priority' na classe do policy-map (estrito e policiado), aplicado à saída com service-policy output.

en.question: Which Cisco offering provides Unified CM-based calling hosted by Cisco as a dedicated private cloud?
options: Cisco Unity Express on branch routers
Webex Calling multi-tenant only
Webex Calling Dedicated Instance
A single on-prem CUBE with SRST
en.explanation: Dedicated Instance runs a customer's own UCM, Unity Connection and Expressway in Webex data centres, managed by Cisco/partner and integrated with Webex.

en.question: Which tool is used to size a Cisco Collaboration deployment (servers and VMs)?
options: The Expressway Configuration Wizard
The Collaboration Sizing Tool
The RTMT Call Flow tool
The Webex Control Hub Analytics page
en.explanation: The Cisco Collaboration Sizing Tool (with the Virtualization guidance) estimates nodes and OVA sizes from users, devices and traffic.

en.question: A G.711 call over Ethernet uses about how much bandwidth per direction, including L2 overhead (20 ms packets)?
options: About 87 kb/s
About 8 kb/s
Exactly 64 kb/s
About 300 kb/s
en.explanation: 64 kb/s payload plus RTP/UDP/IP (40 B) and Ethernet (18 B) headers at 50 pps gives roughly 87 kb/s; G.729 is about 31 kb/s.

en.question: Which audio codec is wideband, adapts its bit rate and is widely used by Webex and modern endpoints?
options: G.711 µ-law
Opus
en.explanation: Opus supports narrowband to fullband, variable bit rate and loss resilience; G.711 is narrowband 64 kb/s.

en.question: How does Unified CM provide call processing redundancy for phones?
options: A single publisher that handles all registration
A CM group of ordered subscribers
An HSRP pair of TFTP servers only
A second cluster with the same IP addresses
en.explanation: The device pool's Unified CM group gives the order of subscribers; phones register to the first and fail over to the next.

en.question: Which UCM feature backs up the cluster configuration for disaster recovery?
options: Disaster Recovery System (DRS)
Bulk Administration Tool export
RTMT trace collection
CDR Analysis and Reporting
en.explanation: DRS backs up the publisher database and components to an SFTP server and restores them after a rebuild.

en.question: Why is SRTP used on collaboration endpoints?
options: It encrypts the voice and video media
It encrypts the SIP signalling only
It compresses RTP headers on WAN links
It authenticates users to LDAP
en.explanation: SRTP protects media confidentiality and integrity; TLS protects SIP signalling, which also carries the SRTP keys (SDES).

en.question: What is the main role of Expressway-C and Expressway-E together?
options: Firewall traversal for remote and B2B
Hosting voicemail boxes for remote users
Replacing UCM as the call control agent
Acting as the cluster's TFTP server
en.explanation: Expressway-E in the DMZ and Expressway-C inside build a traversal zone, enabling Mobile and Remote Access (MRA) and B2B calling without VPN.

en.question: What is CUBE typically used for?
options: A wireless controller for IP phones
A SIP border element for trunks
A presence server for chat and status
An LDAP directory for all users
en.explanation: Cisco Unified Border Element on IOS XE routers demarcates SIP trunks: interworking, security, normalisation and media handling.

en.question: In a UCM cluster upgrade, which node is upgraded first?
options: The TFTP-only node always
Any subscriber in the group
The publisher
All nodes in parallel at once
en.explanation: The publisher is upgraded first, then subscribers (in groups), then a switch version on the publisher before the subscribers.

en.question: SAML SSO for UCM fails with a time-related assertion error. What should be checked first?
options: The CSS of the user's line
The phone button template
NTP on UCM and the IdP
The route list order
en.explanation: SAML assertions have validity windows; clock skew between UCM and the identity provider makes them rejected.

en.question: Why should the Expressway-E certificate be signed by a public CA?
options: It lets phones skip TFTP download
Outside clients must trust it
Public CAs give longer key lengths
Expressway-C requires it for LDAP
en.explanation: MRA clients and B2B partners validate the Expressway-E certificate; SANs must include the MRA domain and other required names.

en.question: What does OAuth with refresh tokens improve for Webex App users on UCM?
options: Higher video resolution on calls
Fewer password prompts
Faster TFTP file download
Automatic dial plan creation
en.explanation: Clients get access and refresh tokens after authenticating, so they reconnect (including over MRA) without re-entering credentials.

en.question: A TLS SIP trunk to CUBE fails during the handshake. Which is a common cause?
options: DTMF is set to KPML
The trunk uses G.711 instead of G.729
The route pattern has no partition
The peer's CA is not trusted
en.explanation: Each side must trust the other's certificate chain (and names must match if checked); otherwise the TLS handshake fails.

en.question: Calls between two secure phones show no lock icon and use RTP. What is a likely reason?
options: The phones have Opus disabled
The phones use the wrong ringtone
The calls route through a hunt pilot
Signalling is not using TLS
en.explanation: SRTP keys are exchanged in signalling; if signalling is not encrypted (TLS) the system falls back to RTP.

en.question: Which DNS record lets Webex App and MRA clients discover Expressway from the internet?
options: PTR record for each phone
A record for the TFTP server
SRV _collab-edge._tls
MX record of the domain
en.explanation: External clients look up _collab-edge._tls.<domain>; internally they look up _cisco-uds._tcp to find UCM.

en.question: Which DHCP option gives Cisco IP phones the TFTP server address?
options: Option 43
Option 150
Option 82
Option 66 only for Cisco
en.explanation: Option 150 lists one or more TFTP servers for Cisco phones (option 66 is the standard single TFTP name).

en.question: How does an IP phone learn its voice VLAN from a Cisco switch?
options: SIP REGISTER messages
DHCP option 150
The TFTP config file
CDP or LLDP-MED
en.explanation: The switch advertises the voice VLAN with CDP (or LLDP-MED); the phone then tags its traffic and requests DHCP in that VLAN.

en.question: Phone users cannot log in to Self Care with their AD passwords, but sync works. What is missing?
options: The user's voicemail profile
LDAP directory sync schedule
A partition on the line
LDAP authentication in UCM
en.explanation: LDAP sync imports users; LDAP authentication must also be enabled so UCM checks passwords against AD.

en.question: What does self-provisioning in UCM allow?
options: Users create route patterns in Self Care
Phones choose their own directory number
Users claim a phone via an IVR
Phones download firmware from the internet
en.explanation: With auto-registration and a self-provisioning IVR, users authenticate with a PIN and the phone is built from their user profile/templates.

en.question: Which UCM tool adds hundreds of phones and users from CSV files?
options: Bulk Administration Tool
Dialed Number Analyzer
Real-Time Monitoring Tool
Disaster Recovery System
en.explanation: BAT uses templates and CSV files to insert, update or delete phones, users and lines in bulk.

en.question: How can a phone be onboarded with an activation code?
options: The code is sent in DHCP option 150
The admin types the MAC into Expressway
The phone scans the network for UCM
The user types the code on the phone
en.explanation: Activation codes avoid entering MACs: the phone contacts the activation service (or UCM) with the code and gets its config, including over MRA.

en.question: Which SIP response indicates the called phone is ringing?
options: 100 Trying
200 OK
180 Ringing
486 Busy Here
en.explanation: 100 Trying is hop-by-hop progress, 180/183 indicate ringing/early media, 200 OK answers; 486 means busy.

en.question: A SIP call is answered but drops after about 30 seconds. What is a typical cause?
options: DTMF uses RFC 2833 payloads
The INVITE has no SDP body
The phone is not registered
The ACK never arrives
en.explanation: Without the ACK, the answering side retransmits 200 OK and tears down after timer expiry (~32 s), often due to NAT/firewall or routing issues.

en.question: What does the SDP 'm=' line describe?
options: The caller's display name
Media type, port, codecs
The SIP server address
The total call duration
en.explanation: m=audio 16384 RTP/AVP 0 101 gives media type, RTP port, transport profile and payload types; c= gives the IP.

en.question: How are DTMF digits sent with RFC 2833/4733?
options: As SIP INFO messages
As RTP telephone events
As in-band audio tones only
As KPML subscriptions
en.explanation: RFC 2833/4733 carries DTMF as RTP payload (commonly type 101), negotiated in SDP; SIP INFO and KPML are signalling methods.

en.question: How does a SIP phone usually place a call on hold?
options: A 486 response to the peer
A BYE followed by a new INVITE
A REGISTER with expires=0
A re-INVITE with sendonly
en.explanation: Hold is a re-INVITE changing the media direction; music on hold may then be inserted; resume sends a re-INVITE with sendrecv.

en.question: Which SIP method is used for a transfer?
options: SUBSCRIBE
REFER
OPTIONS
PRACK
en.explanation: REFER asks the transferee to call the target (with Replaces for attended transfer); NOTIFY reports progress.

en.question: A SIP phone shows 'Registering' and never registers to UCM. Which is a common cause?
options: The device is not configured
The route list has too many members
The phone's CSS lacks the PSTN partition
Music on hold is disabled
en.explanation: Registration needs the device in UCM (or auto-registration), correct TFTP/config and, if used, matching digest credentials; check RTMT and phone logs.

en.question: In UCM, which element decides which partitions a calling device can reach?
options: Calling search space
Media resource group
Device pool
Region between sites
en.explanation: A CSS is an ordered list of partitions; the line CSS and device CSS are combined (line first) for call routing.

en.question: Two route patterns match a dialled number: 9.1XXX and 9.1[2-9]XX. Which one is chosen for 91234?
options: Both, in round-robin
9.1XXX
Neither; the call fails
en.explanation: UCM picks the closest (most specific) match: [2-9] matches 8 values versus 10 for X, so 9.1[2-9]XX wins.

en.question: Which UCM setting helps prevent toll fraud through call forward to international numbers?
options: A restricted forward CSS
A larger region bandwidth
Enabling auto-registration
Using G.711 only on trunks
en.explanation: Restricting the Call Forward All CSS (and blocking international patterns, using FAC and time-of-day) stops users forwarding to expensive numbers.

en.question: What is the difference between a route group and a route list?
options: A route group points to route patterns
They are the same object in UCM
A list orders groups of devices
A route list contains phones
en.explanation: Route pattern → route list (ordered route groups, with local route group) → route group (ordered gateways/trunks with distribution algorithm).

en.question: In a globalized dial plan, where is a called number normalised to +E.164?
options: In the phone's softkey template
On the gateway's POTS dial peer only
In translation patterns on ingress
In the device pool's region
en.explanation: Globalized call routing localises/normalises numbers at ingress (translation patterns, called/calling transformations) and localises at egress.

en.question: What does the local route group (LRG) allow?
options: Assigning phones to partitions
Routing all calls to a single site
Disabling route lists for each site
One pattern, local gateway per site
en.explanation: LRG is bound per device pool, so a single +E.164 route pattern sends calls out the caller's local gateway without per-site patterns.

en.question: How is time-of-day routing configured in UCM?
options: A cron job on the publisher
Time schedules on partitions
A setting in the phone's firmware
A route group distribution algorithm
en.explanation: Time schedules made of time periods are assigned to partitions; outside the schedule, patterns in that partition are not reachable.

en.question: What is a forced authorization code (FAC)?
options: A code for some call types
A PIN for the voicemail box
A licence key for the trunk
A codec negotiation rule
en.explanation: FAC on a route pattern requires an authorisation level code before calls (e.g. international) proceed and logs it in CDRs.

en.question: Why is 'Urgent Priority' set on an emergency route pattern such as 112?
options: It bypasses all partitions
It gives emergency calls higher QoS
It routes without waiting
It records the call for review
en.explanation: Urgent priority stops digit collection on overlap, so 112 routes immediately even if longer patterns like 112X exist.

en.question: Which UCM tool shows how a dialled number would be routed from a given device?
options: Cisco Unified Reporting
Bulk Administration Tool
Disaster Recovery System
Dialed Number Analyzer
en.explanation: DNA simulates digit analysis using the calling device's CSS and shows matched patterns, transformations and the route chosen.

en.question: Which UCM API is SOAP-based and used to provision users, phones and lines?
options: JTAPI
UDS
CTI
AXL
en.explanation: AXL (Administrative XML) is a SOAP/XML API with basic authentication for provisioning; UDS is a REST API mainly for user/device data.

en.question: What does MWI do for a Unity Connection mailbox?
options: Lights the message lamp
Records the user's greeting
Transcribes voicemail to text
Sets the maximum mailbox size
en.explanation: Unity Connection signals UCM (via the SIP/SCCP integration MWI on/off DNs) to light the indicator when there are new messages.

en.question: How is Unity Connection most commonly integrated with UCM today?
options: An analog gateway
SCCP voicemail ports only
H.323 gatekeeper
A SIP trunk
en.explanation: A SIP trunk integration points UCM's voicemail pilot to Unity Connection; SCCP ports are the legacy option.

en.question: In Unity Connection, what decides which call handler answers an incoming call?
options: Routing rules
The phone's CSS
The route list in UCM
The device pool of the port
en.explanation: Routing rules match conditions (calling/dialled number, port, schedule) and send direct or forwarded calls to a call handler, interview handler or conversation.

en.question: How is role-based access given to a helpdesk team in UCM administration?
options: A second publisher node
Separate partitions for each admin
A different device pool
Access control groups
en.explanation: Users (local or LDAP) are added to access control groups whose roles define read/update rights on UCM pages.

en.question: Which dial peer command enables RFC 2833 DTMF relay on a CUBE SIP dial peer?
options: dtmf-relay cisco-rtp sip
dtmf-relay h245-alphanumeric
dtmf-relay rtp-nte
codec dtmf inband
en.explanation: rtp-nte sends named telephone events in RTP; sip-kpml and sip-notify are signalling options; h245 is for H.323.

en.question: A voice translation rule is written as rule 1 /^0\(.*\)/ /+351\1/. What does it do to 0211234567?
options: Changes it to +3510211234567
Changes it to +351211234567
Leaves it unchanged
Deletes all digits
en.explanation: The regex matches a leading 0, captures the rest and replaces it with +351 followed by the captured digits.

en.question: How is a voice translation rule applied to calls on a dial peer?
options: Through a translation profile
Directly with 'rule' on the peer
Via a SIP profile only
Through the codec class
en.explanation: Rules live in a voice translation-rule; a voice translation-profile references them for called/calling numbers and is attached to the dial peer.

en.question: What does a voice class codec list on CUBE define?
options: Ordered codecs to offer
The DSP count for each codec
The bandwidth of the WAN link
The trunk's DTMF method
en.explanation: voice class codec N lists codec preferences; the dial peer references it so CUBE offers/accepts codecs in that order.

en.question: What is the difference between POTS and VoIP dial peers?
options: POTS peers are only for fax calls
POTS: voice ports; VoIP: IP targets
VoIP peers are only for analog phones
There is no practical difference
en.explanation: POTS dial peers use 'port' (FXS/FXO/E1/T1); VoIP dial peers use session target (IP/DNS/server group) and session protocol.

en.question: How does CUBE detect that a SIP trunk peer is down and stop sending calls to it?
options: SIP OPTIONS keepalive
Monitoring BFD sessions to the ITSP
Waiting for the ITSP to send a BYE
Checking the DSP farm status
en.explanation: voice class sip-options-keepalive marks the dial peer busy-out when OPTIONS get no response, so another peer/server group member is used.

en.question: What does a voice class server-group provide on CUBE?
options: Load balancing of DSPs
A cluster of CUBE routers
Many targets per peer
A list of LDAP servers
en.explanation: A server group lists destination IPs with preference or round-robin hunting, referenced by session server-group on the dial peer.

en.question: An inbound call to CUBE matches the wrong inbound dial peer. Which command helps match by a specific URI or IP?
options: dtmf-relay rtp-nte
destination-pattern on the POTS peer
codec preference 1 g711ulaw
incoming uri via
en.explanation: Inbound matching can use incoming uri (from/to/via/request) with a voice class uri, or incoming called/calling numbers; 'show dial-peer voice summary' and debug ccsip help.

en.question: What does a SIP profile on CUBE let you change?
options: The router's routing table
The codec DSP firmware
SIP header normalisation
The phone registration timer
en.explanation: voice class sip-profiles add, modify or remove SIP/SDP headers to interoperate with providers; they are applied per dial peer or globally.

en.question: Why use voice class tenants on a multi-trunk CUBE?
options: To isolate DSPs per customer
Per-provider SIP settings
To bill each department
To license each dial peer
en.explanation: Tenants group global SIP settings (bind, registrar, credentials, timers) per provider so each trunk has its own configuration.

en.question: Which IOS XE media resource is needed for conferencing or transcoding with mixed codecs?
options: A Unity Connection port
An extra SIP trunk
DSP farm resources
A route group
en.explanation: DSP farm profiles (conference, transcode, MTP) register to UCM as media resources and use the router's DSPs.

en.question: Which apps make up the Webex Suite for end users?
options: Only IP phone provisioning
Only video conferencing rooms
Calling, meetings, messaging
Only contact centre agents
en.explanation: The Webex Suite combines calling, meetings, messaging, webinars, polling and more in the Webex App and devices.

en.question: In Webex Calling, how is a call from a user to an external number routed when the location uses a Local Gateway?
options: Via the location's LGW trunk
Directly from the phone to the ITSP
Through the user's mobile carrier
Through Unity Connection
en.explanation: Webex Calling routes PSTN calls per location connection (Cisco PSTN, CCP, or premises-based via a Local Gateway trunk).

en.question: Which Webex Calling feature limits users from placing international calls?
options: Call recording policies
Number masking per user
Calling permissions
Caller ID settings
en.explanation: Calling permissions per location or user allow/block call types (international, premium) and can require authorisation codes.

en.question: In Webex Calling, what is a location?
options: A site with numbers and PSTN
A meeting room device group
A user's home address
A Control Hub admin role
en.explanation: Locations define emergency address, time zone, numbers, PSTN connection and internal dialling settings for users and devices.

en.question: In Webex Calling, how do trunks and route groups relate?
options: Route groups replace dial plans
Trunks contain route groups
They are the same object type
Route groups bundle trunks
en.explanation: Trunks connect to Local Gateways; route groups combine trunks with priorities; dial plans or locations then point to a trunk or route group.

en.question: What is a Webex Calling dial plan used for?
options: Sending patterns to PBX trunks
Assigning numbers to users
Recording all external calls
Changing ringtones per location
en.explanation: Dial plans contain patterns (enterprise numbers) routed to a trunk/route group, letting Webex users reach on-prem UCM or PBX numbers.

en.question: Where are Webex Meetings site settings such as default audio and recording managed?
options: In Unity Connection admin
On each phone's web page
In the UCM route plan
In Control Hub
en.explanation: Meeting sites are configured in Control Hub (formerly Site Admin): audio, recording, security and user privileges.

en.question: Which Control Hub setting can stop users sharing files in Webex messaging with external organisations?
options: Calling permissions
Messaging settings
Meeting site lock
Directory Connector
en.explanation: Control Hub messaging settings include external communication, file sharing restrictions, retention and Pro Pack/Extended Security features.

en.question: What kind of API does Webex expose for developers?
options: REST and JSON
SOAP/XML only
SNMP MIBs only
Telnet CLI only
en.explanation: Webex APIs at webexapis.com are RESTful with JSON bodies, plus SDKs and webhooks.

en.question: How does an integration act on behalf of a Webex user?
options: The user's password in each call
An OAuth 2.0 access token
A shared bot token for everyone
An API key in the URL
en.explanation: Integrations use OAuth authorisation code grant with scopes; bots have their own token; service apps use admin-authorised tokens.

en.question: How does a Webex webhook notify your application?
options: A polling loop in your code
An HTTP POST on each event
A SIP trunk to Webex
A scheduled Control Hub report
en.explanation: You register a webhook (resource + event + targetUrl); Webex calls your endpoint when, for example, a message is created.

en.question: How can users be provisioned into Control Hub automatically from an identity provider like Entra ID?
options: CDR exports
SNMP traps
SCIM
TFTP
en.explanation: SCIM 2.0 from Entra ID/Okta creates and updates users; Directory Connector syncs from on-prem AD. RBAC roles control admin rights.

en.question: What does Webex Cloud-Connected UC (CCUC) provide for on-prem UCM?
options: A free PSTN connection for sites
Moving all users to Webex Calling
Cloud insight into UCM clusters
Replacing Unity Connection
en.explanation: CCUC connects UCM clusters to Control Hub for analytics, certificate management, upgrades insight and other cloud services.

en.question: Which Webex Hybrid Service lets on-prem users schedule Webex meetings from their Exchange/Microsoft 365 calendar?
options: Hybrid Data Security
Hybrid Calendar
Video Mesh
Hybrid Directory only
en.explanation: Hybrid Calendar integrates Exchange, Microsoft 365 or Google calendars to add join buttons (OBTP) and @webex scheduling.

en.question: What does Webex Video Mesh do?
options: Records all calls on-prem
Encrypts messages with local keys
Syncs AD users to the cloud
Keeps meeting media on-prem
en.explanation: Video Mesh nodes host meeting media locally to save internet bandwidth and improve quality, cascading to the cloud when needed.

en.question: A call has one-way audio. What is the most common cause?
options: The codec is G.711 instead of G.722
RTP blocked in one direction
The phone has the wrong ringtone
The user's CSS is wrong
en.explanation: Signalling works but RTP cannot reach one side: missing routes, ACLs, NAT/ALG issues or a wrong media address in SDP.

en.question: Users report choppy audio during busy hours on the WAN. What is the likely cause?
options: Phones use the wrong VLAN name
DNS SRV records are missing
Loss and jitter from congestion
The LDAP sync is delayed
en.explanation: Congestion without QoS causes drops and variable delay; check interface drops, queues and RTP stats (jitter/loss) on phones.

en.question: Which DSCP markings are recommended for voice media and call signalling?
options: Default (0) for both types
AF41 for voice, EF for signalling
CS1 for voice, CS7 for signalling
EF voice, CS3 signalling
en.explanation: Cisco QoS baseline uses EF for voice bearer, CS3 for signalling and AF41 for interactive video.

en.question: Why is QoS on Wi-Fi for voice harder than on wired links?
options: Shared airtime and WMM queues
Wi-Fi does not carry DSCP at all
Wireless only supports G.729
APs cannot use VLANs
en.explanation: WMM maps DSCP/UP to access categories; contention, retries and roaming add jitter, so design for coverage, CAC and fast roaming.

en.question: Where is the trust boundary usually set for a Cisco IP phone with a PC behind it?
options: At the PC's network card
At the IP phone
At the WAN router only
At the internet provider
en.explanation: The access switch extends trust to the phone (via CDP); the phone re-marks PC traffic, so the PC's own markings are not trusted.

en.question: Which configuration creates a low-latency queue for voice on an IOS XE WAN interface?
options: police 64000; match any; service-policy input on LAN
class-map match dscp ef; policy-map bandwidth remaining; service-policy input
access-list 101 permit udp; ip route; interface priority
class-map match dscp ef; policy-map class priority; service-policy output
en.explanation: LLQ uses the 'priority' command in the policy-map class (strict and policed), applied outbound with service-policy output.
